qualifications: Substantial experience of solution design or software engineering, at a level equivalent to a master's degree.

levels.title: Senior solution architect
levels.pcfLevelDescription:
A senior solution architect is responsible for a single, more complex, solution. They usually work on solutions where the risk is moderate. They may lead and coach other solution architects.

At this role level, you will:
- build relationships with senior stakeholders across different business or technical areas in the organisation
- be proactive in identifying opportunities to improve the organisation
- support multiple architecture projects
- find and use emerging technologies and approaches
- support others to follow best practice for solution architecture
responsibilities: Design complex solutions of moderate risk, such as clinical systems or services used across several organisations.
Lead technical evaluation of supplier products in procurements, including interoperability, security, and safety.
Design for resilience and business continuity where the solution supports care around the clock.
Work with clinical safety officers so that design decisions and risk controls are recorded in the safety case.
Coach and review the work of other solution architects.
qualifications: Extensive experience of designing complex solutions, at a level equivalent to a master's degree.

levels.title: Lead solution architect
levels.pcfLevelDescription:
A lead solution architect is responsible for a group of solution architecture projects, or a single more complex area. They may lead teams of more junior solution architects.

At this role level, you will:
- build relationships with senior stakeholders across multiple business or technical areas in the organisation
- be proactive in identifying opportunities to improve the organisation
- support multiple architecture projects or programmes
- find and use emerging technologies and approaches
- develop best practice for solution architecture
responsibilities: Lead the solution architecture for a programme or a complex area, such as an electronic patient record replacement.
Make sure solutions across the programme are consistent, interoperable, and aligned with the target architecture.
Advise programme boards on design risks, dependencies, supplier choices, and costs.
Assure the designs of other solution architects at design authorities.
Lead and develop a team of solution architects.
qualifications: Extensive experience of leading solution architecture for complex programmes.

levels.title: Principal solution architect
levels.pcfLevelDescription:
A principal solution architect can be responsible for a large programme or group of solution architecture projects, or a single, very complex or critical business area.

At this role level, you will:
- lead teams of more junior solution architects
- lead multiple architecture projects or programmes
- build relationships with senior stakeholders across multiple business or technical areas in the organisation and its partners
- be proactive in identifying opportunities to improve the organisation and its partners
- work with technology partners to inform their roadmaps
- take a leading role in the overall direction of business and digital capabilities
- inspire other architects and help them understand how to meet organisational goals
responsibilities: Lead solution architecture for the organisation's largest or most critical programmes.
Set solution architecture standards, patterns, and methods for the organisation.
Advise directors and partner organisations on the design of critical, shared health and care services.
Resolve the hardest design conflicts between programmes, suppliers, and partner organisations.
Lead the solution architecture practice and develop its people.
qualifications: Extensive experience of leading solution architecture across multiple programmes or organisations.

roles.title: Technical architect
roles.summary: Technical architects design the technical structure of the organisation's digital health services: the components, platforms, hosting, integration patterns, and non-functional qualities such as security, performance, and resilience. They work closely with developers and DevOps engineers, give technical leadership to delivery teams, and make sure services are built to last and safe to run.
healthContext: Clinical services often need high availability and fast recovery, so technical designs must plan for failure and degraded running.
Designs must protect confidential health information through encryption, access control, and audit by default.
Services connect to many clinical systems and shared platforms, often through HL7 FHIR APIs and messaging, so integration patterns are central to the design.
Technical design choices, such as caching, retries, and time handling, can cause clinical hazards, so architects contribute to safety cases.
Legacy clinical systems and medical devices may constrain choices of technology, networking, and hosting.

pcfRole.name: Technical architect
pcfRole.description: A technical architect provides technical leadership and architectural design.

levels.title: Associate technical architect
levels.pcfLevelDescription:
An associate technical architect supports technical architects in putting forward designs as solutions to technology challenges, usually under supervision.

At this role level, you will:
- work closely with developers when designing appropriate solutions
- have an understanding of the overall strategy and how your work supports it
responsibilities: Draw technical diagrams and document the components, hosting, and integrations of existing services.
Research technology options and summarise their pros and cons, with guidance.
Work with developers to check that builds follow agreed designs and patterns.
Record technical decisions and keep design documents up to date.
qualifications: A degree in computing or a related subject, or equivalent experience in software or infrastructure engineering.

levels.title: Technical architect
levels.pcfLevelDescription:
A technical architect is responsible for the design and build of technical architecture.

At this role level, you will:
- undertake structured analysis of technical issues, translating this analysis into technical designs that describe a solution
- be consulted about design and provide design patterns
- identify deeper issues that need fixing
- look for opportunities to collaborate and reuse components, communicating with both technical and non-technical stakeholders
responsibilities: Design the technical architecture for a service, including components, hosting, integration, and security.
Provide design patterns to delivery teams and review their technical designs and code structure.
Define non-functional requirements, such as availability, performance, and recovery targets, with service owners.
Identify technical debt and unsupported technology, and plan how to fix it.
Identify technical hazards and controls for the clinical safety case.
qualifications: A degree in computing or a related subject, or equivalent experience.
Experience of designing or building production software or infrastructure.
levels.jobEvaluationNotes: The UK GDaD PCF suggests Band 7 for both technical architect and senior technical architect; this reference places the technical architect level at Band 6, at the lower end of its grade range, to avoid two levels in one band.

levels.title: Senior technical architect
levels.pcfLevelDescription:
A senior technical architect works on large or multiple pieces of work that are complex or risky.

At this role level, you will:
- define strategy and be central to assuring services
- regularly collaborate and find agreement with senior stakeholders, providing direction and challenge
- be proactive in identifying problems and translating these into non-technical descriptions that can be widely understood
- mentor and coach junior colleagues
responsibilities: Lead the technical design of large, complex, or high-risk services, such as clinical systems and shared integration platforms.
Set technical direction for one or more delivery teams and challenge designs that add risk.
Design for resilience, disaster recovery, and secure running, and check that teams test it.
Explain technical risks and trade-offs to service owners, clinical leads, and senior stakeholders in plain language.
Mentor and coach technical architects and senior developers.
qualifications: Substantial experience of technical design for complex services, at a level equivalent to a master's degree.

levels.title: Lead technical architect
levels.pcfLevelDescription:
A lead technical architect works with multiple projects or teams on problems that require broad architectural thinking.

At this role level, you will:
- be responsible for leading the technical design of systems and services, justifying and communicating design decisions
- assure other services and system quality, ensuring the technical work fits into the broader strategy for government
- explore the benefits of cross-government alignment
- provide mentoring within teams
- provide leadership to other architects
responsibilities: Lead the technical architecture across several services or teams, setting shared patterns and standards.
Assure the technical quality of designs at design authorities, including security, resilience, and interoperability.
Shape the organisation's technology roadmap with enterprise architects and engineering leads.
Advise senior leaders on technology choices, platform investment, and technical risk.
Lead and develop technical architects.
qualifications: Extensive experience of leading technical architecture for complex services.

levels.title: Principal technical architect
levels.pcfLevelDescription:
A principal technical architect leads at the highest level and is responsible for making sure the strategy is agreed and followed.

At this role level, you will:
- network and communicate with senior stakeholders across organisations
- proactively seek opportunities for digital transformation
- support multiple teams, finding and using best practice and emerging technologies
- inspire other architects and help them understand how to deliver the goals of the organisation
- be responsible for governance, solving complex and high risk issues or delivering architecture design
responsibilities: Set the organisation's technical architecture strategy, principles, and standards.
Govern technical design across the organisation, including the technical design authority.
Advise the executive team on major technology decisions, such as hosting strategy and platform consolidation.
Represent the organisation in cross-organisation technical and standards communities.
Inspire and develop architects across the organisation.
qualifications: Extensive experience of leading technical architecture across multiple teams or organisations.

roles.title: Data architect
roles.summary: Data architects design how the organisation structures, stores, moves, and governs its health and care data, so that it can be used safely for direct care, service planning, and research. They design data models, data platforms, and data flows, set data standards, and make sure clinical meaning, quality, and confidentiality are kept from end to end.
healthContext: Health data must keep its clinical meaning, so data models use clinical terminologies such as SNOMED CT and classifications such as ICD.
Data used for direct care and data used for planning or research have different legal bases, so architects design for separation, de-identification, and controlled access.
Data comes from many clinical and care systems of varying quality, so architects design for data quality checks, patient matching, and lineage.
Shared care records and data exchange depend on common models such as HL7 FHIR resources and agreed national or international datasets.
Records must be kept for long retention periods, so designs must plan for archiving and access to historical data.

pcfRole.name: Data architect
pcfRole.description: A data architect sets the vision for the organisation’s use of data, through data design, to ensure that data is managed properly and meets the organisation’s needs.

levels.title: Data architect
levels.pcfLevelDescription:
A data architect designs and builds data models to fulfil the strategic data needs of the organisation, as defined by chief data architects.

At this role level, you will:
- design, support and provide guidance for the upgrade, management, decommission and archive of data in compliance with data policy
- provide input into data dictionaries
- define and maintain the data technology architecture, including metadata, integration and business intelligence or data warehouse architecture
responsibilities: Design logical and physical data models for clinical and operational data, using clinical terminologies where needed.
Design data flows and data platform components, such as warehouse, lakehouse, and integration layers.
Define metadata, data dictionary entries, and lineage for the datasets in your area.
Design de-identification and access controls so that data is used only for its lawful purpose.
Work with data quality and clinical coding colleagues to fix structural causes of poor data.
qualifications: Substantial experience of data modelling and data platform design, at a level equivalent to a master's degree.

levels.title: Senior data architect
levels.pcfLevelDescription:
A senior data architect delivers the vision for the organisation as set by the chief data architect.

At this role level, you will:
- design data models and metadata systems
- help chief data architects to interpret an organisation’s needs
- provide oversight and advice to other data architects who are designing and producing data artefacts
- design and support the management of data dictionaries
- make sure that your teams are working to the standards set for the organisation by the chief data architects
- work with technical architects to make sure that an organisation’s systems are designed in accordance with the appropriate data architecture
responsibilities: Design the data architecture for a major domain, such as the shared care record or the analytics platform.
Make sure data designs across teams follow the organisation's data standards and models.
Design how data is shared with partner organisations, including standards, controls, and data sharing agreements.
Advise information governance and clinical safety colleagues on the data risks of new designs.
Review and guide the work of data architects.
qualifications: Extensive experience of data architecture for complex organisations.

levels.title: Chief data architect
levels.pcfLevelDescription:
A chief data architect sets the vision for the organisation’s use of data as directed by the appropriate governance body.

At this role level, you will:
- oversee the design of multiple data models and have a broad understanding of how each model fulfils the needs of the organisation
- be accountable for supporting and aligning to the organisation’s data strategy
- champion data architecture both internally and through collaborating and communicating at the most senior levels across government
- set the standards and ways of working for the data architecture community
- be accountable for assuring data models at the level of a project or enterprise
- provide advice to project teams and oversee the management of the full data product life cycle
- be responsible for ensuring that the organisation’s systems are designed in accordance with the enterprise data architecture
responsibilities: Set the organisation's data architecture vision and roadmap, in line with its data strategy.
Own the organisation's enterprise data model, data standards, and data dictionary.
Advise the executive team and data governance bodies on data architecture, risks, and investment.
Represent the organisation in cross-organisation data standards and interoperability work.
Lead the data architecture practice and develop its people.
qualifications: Extensive experience of leading data architecture across organisations.

roles.title: Security architect
roles.summary: Security architects design the security of the organisation's digital health services, so that patient information stays confidential, accurate, and available when care needs it. They set security patterns and controls, assess the security risk of new designs and suppliers, and help teams make risk-based decisions that keep services both safe and usable for clinicians and patients.
healthContext: Health organisations are frequent targets of ransomware and data theft, and an attack can stop clinical services, so availability is as important as confidentiality.
Security controls must not get in the way of urgent care, so designs balance strong authentication with fast access in clinical settings.
Connected medical devices and legacy clinical systems often cannot be patched quickly, so architects design compensating controls such as segmentation.
Many staff, partner organisations, and suppliers need access to patient records, so identity, role-based access, and audit are central.
Security designs must support information governance duties and published security standards, such as ISO/IEC 27001.

pcfRole.name: Security architect
pcfRole.description: A security architect designs and builds secure solutions.

levels.title: Security architect
levels.pcfLevelDescription:
A security architect creates and designs security for a system or service, maintains security documentation and develops architecture patterns and security approaches to new technologies.

At this role level, you will:
- recommend security controls and identify solutions that support a business objective
- provide specialist advice and recommend approaches across teams and various stakeholders
- communicate widely with other stakeholders
- advise on important security-related technologies and assess the risk associated with proposed changes
- inspire and influence others to execute security principles
- help review other people’s work
responsibilities: Design security controls for services and systems, including identity, encryption, logging, and network protection.
Assess the security of new designs and supplier products, and record risks and recommended controls.
Develop security patterns that delivery teams can reuse, such as for patient login and staff single sign-on.
Advise on compensating controls for medical devices and legacy clinical systems that cannot be updated easily.
Work with information governance and clinical safety colleagues so that security, privacy, and safety risks are assessed together.
qualifications: Substantial experience of security architecture or security engineering, at a level equivalent to a master's degree.
A recognised security qualification or equivalent experience.
levels.jobEvaluationNotes: The UK GDaD PCF suggests Band 6 for this level, which spans HEO to G7; this reference places it at Band 7, at the upper end of its grade range, because the job designs security for critical clinical systems with limited supervision, and to narrow the gap to the lead level at Band 8b.

levels.title: Lead security architect
levels.pcfLevelDescription:
A lead security architect undertakes complex work of a high risk level, often working on several projects.

At this role level, you will:
- interact with senior stakeholders across departments
- reach and influence a wide range of people across larger teams and communities
- research and apply innovative security architecture solutions to new or existing problems and be able to justify and communicate design decisions
- develop vision, principles and strategy for security architects for one project or technology
- work out subtle security needs
- understand the impact of decisions, balancing requirements and deciding between approaches
- produce particular patterns and support quality assurance
- be the point of escalation for architects in lower grade roles
- lead the technical design of systems and services
responsibilities: Lead security architecture for several high-risk projects or a major area, such as clinical systems or cloud hosting.
Set security principles and standards for designs in your area and assure them at design authorities.
Advise senior risk owners on security risks and the options to manage them.
Design security for data shared with partner organisations and suppliers.
Lead and develop security architects.
qualifications: Extensive experience of security architecture for complex services.

levels.title: Principal security architect
levels.pcfLevelDescription:
A principal security architect works on services of high complexity and risk, making decisions to enable the business to achieve its needs.

At this role level, you will:
- work on projects with high strategic impact, setting a strategy that can be used in the long term and across the breadth of the organisation
- communicate with a broad range of senior stakeholders and be responsible for defining the vision, principles and strategy for security architects
- recommend security design across several projects or technologies, up to an organisational or inter-organisational level
- have a deep and evolving level of technical expertise, so you can act as an exemplar
- make and influence important business and architectural decisions
- research, identify, validate and adopt new technologies and methodologies
- be a recognised expert and demonstrate this expertise by solving unprecedented issues and problems
- further the profession, demonstrating and sharing best practice within and outside the organisation
responsibilities: Set the organisation's security architecture vision, principles, and strategy.
Advise the executive team and board on cyber security risk to patient care and services.
Make sure cyber resilience, including recovery from a major attack, is designed into critical clinical services.
Represent the organisation in cross-organisation cyber security and standards communities.
Lead the security architecture practice and develop its people.
qualifications: Extensive experience of leading security architecture across organisations.

roles.title: Network architect
roles.summary: Network architects design the local, wide area, wireless, and cloud networks that connect the organisation's sites, staff, clinical systems, and medical devices. They make sure networks are fast, resilient, and secure enough for care that never stops, and they plan how networks change as services move to the cloud and connect with partner organisations.
healthContext: Clinical systems, telephony, and medical devices depend on the network, so an outage can stop care; designs need resilience and tested failover.
Networks often carry connected medical devices that are hard to patch, so architects design segmentation and monitoring to protect them.
Staff work across hospitals, clinics, community settings, and patients' homes, so designs must support secure mobile and remote access.
Networks connect to shared health and care networks and partner organisations, which set their own connection and security requirements.
Changes to clinical areas need careful planning around patient care, for example scheduling work outside busy periods.

pcfRole.name: Network architect
pcfRole.description: A network architect is responsible for network designs and specifications, including cloud networks.

levels.title: Associate network architect
levels.pcfLevelDescription:
An associate network architect works with network architects on designs and specifications, with guidance.

At this role level, you will:
- be aware and knowledgeable of new technology solutions and produce network design policy
- draft recommendations for network support, creating and maintaining network plans and planning infrastructure runs
- ensure designs meet SLAs (service level agreements) and develop an understanding of common tools
- have an understanding of one or two of the following network technologies: LAN (local area network), WAN (wide area network), wifi, data centre LAN, SD (software-defined) networks, telephony, mobile solutions infrastructure, unified comms, network management solutions, network specific security and remote access technologies and approaches
- collaborate with engineers to ensure systems are practically designed
responsibilities: Draft network designs, diagrams, and specifications with guidance from network architects.
Survey sites and gather requirements for clinical areas, including wireless coverage and device connections.
Keep records of network topology, addressing, and connected devices up to date.
Check that designs meet service levels and security standards before review.
qualifications: A degree in computing or networking, a recognised networking qualification, or equivalent experience.

levels.title: Network architect
levels.pcfLevelDescription:
A network architect has responsibility for network designs and specifications to support business strategies using common tools.

At this role level, you will:
- research new technologies and solutions, and ensure appropriate levels of assurance
- plan, direct and co-ordinate activities, engaging with other stakeholders to manage and implement a programme
- agree SLAs (service level agreements) and engage with third party vendors
- have an understanding of most of the following network technologies: LAN (local area network), WAN (wide area network), wifi, data-centre LAN, SD (software-defined) networks, telephony, mobile solutions infrastructure, unified comms, network management solutions, network-specific security and remote access technologies and approaches
- coach and mentor associate network architects where appropriate
- collaborate with engineers to ensure systems are practically designed
responsibilities: Design local, wide area, wireless, and cloud network solutions for sites and services.
Design network segmentation for medical devices, clinical systems, and guest access.
Plan network changes in clinical areas with service leads so that care is not disrupted.
Agree service levels with suppliers and connection requirements with partner networks.
Assess new network technologies and their fit with the organisation's security standards.
qualifications: A degree in computing or networking, or equivalent experience.
Experience of designing and supporting enterprise networks.

levels.title: Lead network architect
levels.pcfLevelDescription:
A lead network architect is accountable for designs and networks representing their business area.

At this role level, you will:
- be a point of escalation
- actively input into governance forums that determine IT strategy
- cascade messages, standards and best practice from other architecture teams and design authorities to the network architecture team
- act as a subject matter expert for network architects
- represent network architects internally and externally
- have an understanding of all network technology including LAN (local area network), WAN (wide area network), wifi, data centre LAN, SD (software-defined) networks, telephony, mobile solutions infrastructure, unified comms, network management solutions, and network specific security and remote access technologies and approaches
- champion new technologies and solutions
- coach and mentor network architects and associate network architects
- be a strategic thinker who can communicate network concepts to technical and non-technical stakeholders
responsibilities: Own the network architecture for the organisation, including its sites, data centres, and cloud connections.
Set network design standards and assure designs at the design authority.
Design network resilience and recovery for critical clinical services, and make sure it is tested.
Advise on network investment, supplier contracts, and the network risks of new services.
Act as the expert point of escalation and guide other network architects and engineers.
qualifications: Substantial experience of network architecture for complex organisations, at a level equivalent to a master's degree.

roles.title: Business architect
roles.summary: Business architects build a clear, joined-up view of how the organisation delivers health and care: its capabilities, services, care pathways, processes, and information. They use that view to show where change is needed, to connect strategy with programmes, and to make sure digital change improves care for patients and the working lives of clinicians and care staff.
healthContext: Care pathways cross teams, settings, and organisations, so business architects model services from the patient's point of view, not only by department.
Change in clinical processes can affect patient safety and staff workload, so models are built with clinicians and care staff and checked against real practice.
Health and care strategy is shaped by policy, regulation, and funding rules, which architects must translate into practical capability changes.
Many capabilities are shared with partner organisations, so architects help agree who does what and where information must flow.

pcfRole.name: Business architect
pcfRole.description:
A business architect develops an integrated view of an enterprise, such as a business area or organisation. They use this view to help their organisation put its strategy in place.

In this role, you will:
- understand and apply business architectural principles, techniques, and tools to business challenges
- ensure design work from projects and programmes aligns with strategy
- ensure business change is implemented effectively to meet strategy
- aggregate and disaggregate complex information from across your organisation
- communicate complex information about the organisation to stakeholders

levels.title: Trainee business architect
levels.pcfLevelDescription:
A trainee business architect supports the more senior business architect roles. They also receive training on the tasks they support so they can work on their own.

At this role level, you will:
- develop your knowledge of the frameworks, practice, and principles of business architecture
- work with other business architects to support the production of clear business architecture outputs
- support during workshops and meetings with stakeholders in the organisation
responsibilities: Learn business architecture methods, such as capability, value stream, and process modelling, through training and practice.
Gather information about services and care pathways through interviews, documents, and observation.
Draft capability maps and process models with guidance from business architects.
Help run workshops with clinicians, care staff, and managers, and write up the outputs.
qualifications: A degree or equivalent experience in business, analysis, or a related subject.

levels.title: Associate business architect
levels.pcfLevelDescription:
An associate business architect uses their knowledge and experience to address business scenarios. They continue to get support and training for their role.

At this role level, you will:
- apply architectural methods following direction and wider strategy to produce outputs
- break down complexity and produce clear outputs
- explain complex business problems using clear language and artefacts
- bring together disconnected information to inform decision making
- recognise issues that cut across different areas of the organisation and present opportunities for improvement
responsibilities: Model capabilities, services, and care pathways for a part of the organisation.
Analyse models to find gaps, duplication, and pain points for patients and staff.
Bring together information from different teams and organisations to inform decisions on change.
Explain complex service problems to stakeholders using clear models and plain language.
Keep the business architecture repository accurate and linked to application and data models.
qualifications: A degree or equivalent experience in business, analysis, or a related subject.
Experience of business analysis or service design.

levels.title: Business architect
levels.pcfLevelDescription:
A business architect uses their knowledge and experience to understand business scenarios, communicate the issues and recommend next steps. They support and guide other business architects.

At this role level, you will:
- support executive level work and management of the business architecture practice
- guide others in using appropriate business architectural tools and methods
- understand and apply business architectural principles, techniques, and tools to business scenarios
- create business architecture artefacts, including abstract representations of the organisation, knowing when to apply them
- develop standard and scalable models to collect, aggregate, or disaggregate complex information
responsibilities: Develop current and target business architectures for a major service area, such as urgent care or community services.
Translate strategy and policy into capability changes and a roadmap of change.
Check that programme and project scope fits the target business architecture.
Work with clinical leads to assess how proposed changes affect care pathways, safety, and staff workload.
Guide other business architects in methods and tools.
qualifications: Substantial experience of business architecture, business analysis, or service design, at a level equivalent to a master's degree.

levels.title: Lead business architect
levels.pcfLevelDescription:
A lead business architect uses their expert knowledge and experience to direct the work addressing high level and complex business scenarios. They support and lead other business architects.

At this role level, you will:
- be accountable for outputs produced by the business architecture team
- lead and direct the application of architectural principles, methods, and tools to business scenarios
- use architectural methods to form a view of the whole enterprise in a way that is easily understood by stakeholders
- work with stakeholders at executive levels
- provide overall direction, guidance, and definition of business architecture to support strategy
- develop and maintain a strong business architecture capability through coaching, mentoring, and training
responsibilities: Lead the business architecture practice and be accountable for its outputs.
Maintain the organisation-wide view of capabilities, services, and care pathways, and keep it easy to understand.
Advise directors on the priorities for change and how investment portfolios fit strategy.
Work with partner organisations to agree shared capabilities and responsibilities across care pathways.
Lead and develop business architects.
qualifications: Extensive experience of leading business architecture in a complex organisation.

roles.title: Data analyst
roles.summary: Data analysts turn health and care data into information that helps clinicians, managers, and planners make decisions. They prepare, link, and analyse data from clinical, operational, and patient-reported sources, and present it in reports, dashboards, and briefings. They make sure their analysis is accurate, reproducible, and handles confidential patient data safely.
healthContext: Much of the data describes individual patients, so analysts work with pseudonymised data where they can and check outputs for disclosure risk before release.
Health data is recorded with clinical terminologies and classifications such as SNOMED CT and ICD, so analysts need to know how codes are used and where they can mislead.
Data quality varies between care settings and systems, and gaps often affect some patient groups more than others, so analysts check for bias before drawing conclusions.
Analysis can change how services are planned, funded, and delivered, so findings need clear caveats and must not overstate certainty.

pcfRole.name: Data analyst
pcfRole.description:
A data analyst collects, manages, explores and shares data to support organisational objectives and deliver business impact.

In this role, you will:
- identify, collect and move data between a range of systems
- apply data analysis and data visualisation tools and techniques
- prepare, manage and model data, following appropriate standards and practices
- communicate data, insights and conclusions in appropriate formats

levels.title: Associate data analyst
levels.pcfLevelDescription:
An associate data analyst supports data analysis activities and projects. They develop their skills in data analysis by working closely with other data professionals.

At this role level, you will:
- support the development and delivery of data analysis and data projects
- develop analytical approaches and data visualisations, under supervision
- work with others to understand roles within a multi-disciplinary team and how data analysts work with them
responsibilities: Produce routine reports and dashboards on activity, waiting times, and service use, following agreed methods.
Clean and prepare extracts from patient administration, clinical, and operational systems under supervision.
Check outputs against data quality rules and report problems to the right data owner.
Apply small number suppression and other disclosure rules before sharing results.
Answer straightforward data requests from clinical and operational teams.
qualifications: A degree in a numerate subject, an analytics apprenticeship, or equivalent experience.

levels.title: Data analyst
levels.pcfLevelDescription:
A data analyst contributes to the planning, analysis and implementation of data. They work to appropriate standards and ensure data is used to achieve the team's goals.

At this role level, you will:
- prepare and manage data
- apply appropriate techniques, tools and processes to effectively analyse data
- communicate data to stakeholders with different needs
responsibilities: Design and carry out analyses that answer questions from clinical, operational, and planning teams.
Link patient-level data from different sources safely, using pseudonymised identifiers and agreed linkage methods.
Write reproducible analysis code and document methods, assumptions, and data sources.
Explain findings and their limits to clinicians and managers in plain language.
Check analysis for bias across patient groups, such as by age, sex, ethnicity, and deprivation.
Support associate analysts and review their work.
qualifications: A degree in a numerate subject, or equivalent experience.
Experience of analysing and presenting complex data.

levels.title: Senior data analyst
levels.pcfLevelDescription:
A senior data analyst leads data analysis in a team or across an area. They ensure data is appropriately prepared, managed and used, and that data analysis outcomes align with the organisation's goals.

At this role level, you will:
- guide others in appropriate practices for preparing, managing and using data
- lead the application and improvement of processes and ways of working with data
- lead communication of data and data projects with stakeholders, adapting to their needs and requirements
responsibilities: Lead analysis for a service area, such as urgent care, cancer, or mental health, agreeing priorities with its leaders.
Set methods and quality assurance for the team's analysis, including peer review of code and outputs.
Lead complex linkage projects across care settings and agree their information governance basis.
Present findings to senior clinical and management groups and advise on what they mean for services.
Work with data engineers and data owners to fix the root causes of poor data quality.
Coach and develop analysts in the team.
qualifications: Substantial experience of leading data analysis, at a level equivalent to a master's degree.

levels.title: Principal data analyst
levels.pcfLevelDescription:
A principal data analyst leads teams or significant areas of work in data analysis. They determine and implement appropriate standards, processes and structures to ensure data is prepared, managed and used effectively within the organisation.

At this role level, you will:
- influence organisational decision making on data analysis and the use of data
- oversee continuous improvement of the organisation's data practices and management
- represent the data analyst community inside and outside of the organisation
responsibilities: Set the organisation's standards for data analysis, quality assurance, and reproducible analytical practice.
Advise executive and clinical leaders on the evidence behind major decisions about services and investment.
Lead the analytical community, including its training, tools, and career development.
Shape data sharing and linkage arrangements with health and care partners.
Line manage senior analysts and make sure the team has the capacity and skills it needs.
qualifications: Extensive experience of leading data analysis across an organisation.

roles.title: Performance analyst
roles.summary: Performance analysts measure how well the organisation's digital health services work for patients, service users, clinicians, and care staff. They set up measurement frameworks, collect and analyse usage and outcome data, and help product teams and service leaders understand whether changes improve access, experience, safety, and efficiency.
healthContext: Success measures go beyond digital take-up, to include effects on care, such as missed appointments, waiting times, safe triage, and staff time released.
Analytics and tracking on health services can reveal sensitive information, such as which condition a person searched for, so measurement must respect consent, cookie rules, and confidentiality.
Digital services must not widen health inequalities, so analysts look at take-up and outcomes for groups who are less likely to use digital services.
Performance data may be reported to boards, commissioners, and regulators, so definitions must be consistent and well documented.

pcfRole.name: Performance analyst
pcfRole.description: A performance analyst conducts analysis. In this role, you will develop performance measurement frameworks - Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), goals, user needs and benefits - and analyse the performance of a service or product against these, adapting your approach and framework appropriately and in line with any changes.

levels.title: Associate performance analyst
levels.pcfLevelDescription:
An associate performance analyst is an entry-level role requiring numeracy and some experience in analysis or data handling.

At this role level, you will:
- have the aptitude to learn to use analytical tools and produce standardised reports and charts
- start by working on projects with limited scope under the guidance of performance analysts and more senior role levels, replicating existing analysis and data techniques
- progress to greater independence (where appropriate)
- have the opportunity to develop an understanding of the wider analytics context, tools and techniques
- be responsible for the accuracy and quality of data and analysis, and how they are used
- engage with the performance analysis community
responsibilities: Produce regular reports on how patients and staff use digital services, such as sign-ups, completions, and drop-out points.
Check analytics and tracking data for gaps and errors, and report them to the team.
Follow the organisation's rules on consent and confidentiality when collecting and sharing usage data.
Help product teams answer simple questions about service use.
qualifications: Good numeracy and some experience of handling or analysing data, or equivalent.

levels.title: Performance analyst
levels.pcfLevelDescription:
A performance analyst has a strong understanding of a wide range of sources and analytical tools needed for the project they are working on.

At this role level, you will:
- be responsible for the performance analysis in your given area
- help the project team measure and assess outcomes (for example, what good looks like and how it will be measured)
- help to plan and ensure project delivery
- find opportunities to share information with the project team, community colleagues and others
- work independently, but know to seek guidance when necessary
- be adaptable in applying analysis techniques to new contexts, especially when acting as the sole representative for performance analysts on a project
- create a performance measurement framework for a project with the wider team, including identifying reporting requirements, advising on procurement, implementation and validation of tools to deliver against these requirements
- be responsible for the accuracy and quality of data and analysis, and how they are used
- be engaged with, and actively contribute to, the performance analysis community
responsibilities: Agree with product teams and clinical leads what success looks like for a service, including effects on care and on staff.
Set up and validate analytics, so that tracking is accurate, proportionate, and respects consent.
Combine digital analytics with operational data, such as appointments and referrals, to show the effect of changes.
Analyse take-up and outcomes for different patient groups and highlight risks of digital exclusion.
Present findings to product teams and service leaders and recommend improvements.
qualifications: A degree in a numerate subject, or equivalent experience.
Experience of measuring the performance of digital services.

levels.title: Senior performance analyst
levels.pcfLevelDescription:
A senior performance analyst looks to delegate, automate or upskill others in analysis where possible and appropriate, provide leadership within their team and proactively use analysis to improve services.

At this role level, you will:
- potentially manage one or more performance analysts
- be proficient in a wide range of tools
- ensure the team is equipped with the required skills according to the strategy set out by the head of performance analysis
- be skilled and experienced at carrying out the day-to-day activities of a performance analyst, including setting up performance measurement frameworks
- carry out increasingly complex analysis, working with other teams where necessary
- actively contribute to the performance analysis community within your department or organisation, while forging links with other analytical disciplines
As a 'technical specialist senior performance analyst', you would look to develop tools and techniques to aid others in analysis. You would be responsible for the accuracy and quality of data and analysis, and for how data and analysis are used.
responsibilities: Lead performance measurement for a group of services or a major programme, such as digital outpatients or online triage.
Design benefits measures with clinical, finance, and operational leads, and track them through delivery.
Choose and configure analytics tools that meet information governance and security requirements.
Present performance evidence to programme boards and senior leaders.
Coach analysts and may line manage one or more performance analysts.
qualifications: Substantial experience of performance analysis for digital services, at a level equivalent to a master's degree.

levels.title: Lead performance analyst
levels.pcfLevelDescription:
A lead performance analyst manages junior performance analysts at any level, co-ordinating teams or groups of related analysts.

At this role level, you will:
- assist, take forward and influence the strategy as determined by the head of performance analysis, including data implementation and data architecture
- remove blockers and act as an escalation point for important issues
- be an ambassador for analytics across communities, departments and government
- be responsible for the accuracy and quality of data and analysis, and of how data and analysis are used
- proactively share knowledge and promote a data-driven culture, as a leader in the community
- coach and mentor senior performance analysts, performance analysts and associate performance analysts
responsibilities: Lead a team of performance analysts across a portfolio of digital health services.
Agree consistent definitions for key performance measures, so reports to boards and partners can be compared over time.
Make sure analytics data is accurate, used appropriately, and handled in line with information governance rules.
Use performance evidence to influence portfolio priorities and investment.
Coach and mentor analysts at all levels.
qualifications: Extensive experience of performance analysis and of leading analysts.

levels.title: Head of performance analysis
levels.pcfLevelDescription:
The head of performance analysis leads the performance analysis community, acting as the point of contact between the community and the business.

At this role level, you will:
- remove blockers and act as an escalation point for important issues
- set the performance analysis strategy with input from lead and senior performance analysts
- be responsible for defining a framework for quality assurance within performance analysis
- champion performance analysis and performance analysts, working with colleagues across government and other Government Digital and Data communities and analytical professions
- manage the organisation’s performance analysis capability through business planning, development and recruitment
responsibilities: Set the strategy for measuring the performance and benefits of the organisation's digital services.
Define the quality assurance framework for performance analysis and performance reporting.
Advise executive leaders on what performance evidence shows about digital services and patient outcomes.
Work with other analytical professions, such as data analysis and data science, to share methods and data.
Plan the capability of the performance analysis community, including recruitment and development.
qualifications: Extensive experience of leading performance analysis across an organisation.

roles.title: Data engineer
roles.summary: Data engineers build and run the pipelines and platforms that move health and care data from clinical and operational systems into places where it can be analysed and used safely. They design data flows, integrate sources that use different standards, and make sure data is accurate, timely, secure, and only available to the people who should see it.
healthContext: Source systems include electronic patient records, laboratory, imaging, and pharmacy systems, which use standards such as HL7 version 2, HL7 FHIR, SNOMED CT, and ICD.
Pipelines often carry identifiable patient data, so engineers build in pseudonymisation, access control, and audit from the start.
Some data feeds support direct care, such as alerts or patient lists, so a failed or late pipeline can affect patients and needs clinical safety assessment.
Data often needs linking across care settings, which depends on reliable patient matching and consistent identifiers.

pcfRole.name: Data engineer
pcfRole.description: A data engineer develops and constructs data products and services, and integrates them into systems and business processes.

levels.title: Data engineer
levels.pcfLevelDescription:
A data engineer delivers the designs set by more senior members of the data engineering community.

At this role level, you will:
- implement data flows to connect operational systems, data for analytics and business intelligence (BI) systems
- document source-to-target mappings
- re-engineer manual data flows to enable scaling and repeatable use
- support the build of data streaming systems
- write ETL (extract, transform, load) scripts and code to ensure the ETL process performs optimally
- develop business intelligence reports that can be reused
- build accessible data for analysis
responsibilities: Build and maintain data pipelines from clinical and operational systems to the data platform, following agreed designs.
Map source data, including coded clinical data, to target models and document the mappings.
Build pseudonymisation, validation, and data quality checks into pipelines.
Monitor pipelines and fix failures, prioritising feeds that support direct care.
Apply access controls and audit logging that meet information governance rules.
qualifications: A degree in computing or a related subject, or equivalent experience.
Experience of building data pipelines.

levels.title: Senior data engineer
levels.pcfLevelDescription:
A senior data engineer designs and leads the implementation of data flows to connect operational systems, data for analytics and business intelligence (BI) systems.

At this role level, you will:
- recognise opportunities to reuse existing data flows
- lead the build of data streaming systems
- optimise the code to ensure processes perform optimally
- lead work on database management
responsibilities: Design data flows and streaming services that bring together data from many health and care systems.
Design patient matching and linkage processes, and measure how well they work.
Lead database and platform performance work so data is available when services need it.
Assess the clinical safety and information governance risks of data flows with the relevant specialists.
Review the work of other engineers and coach them.
qualifications: Substantial experience of designing and building data systems, at a level equivalent to a master's degree.

levels.title: Lead data engineer
levels.pcfLevelDescription:
A lead data engineer is responsible for the design and implementation of numerous complex data flows to connect operational systems, data for analytics and business intelligence (BI) systems.

At this role level, you will:
- recognise and share opportunities to reuse existing data flows between teams
- be responsible for the build of data-streaming systems
- co-ordinate teams and set best practice and standards
- apply knowledge of systems integration to your work
- champion data engineering across government
responsibilities: Lead the design and running of the organisation's data platform and its many data flows.
Set engineering standards for pipelines, testing, security, and documentation.
Plan data integration with health and care partners, including shared care records and regional data services.
Make sure data flows that support direct care are resilient and have clinical safety cases.
Coordinate data engineering teams and line manage engineers.
qualifications: Extensive experience of leading data engineering for complex systems.

levels.title: Head of data engineering
levels.pcfLevelDescription:
A head of data engineering leads multi-functional delivery teams to deliver robust data services for their department, other government departments and private sector partners.

At this role level, you will:
- inspire best practice for data products and services within your teams
- build data engineering capability by providing technical leadership and career development for the community
- work with other senior team members to identify, plan, develop and deliver data services
responsibilities: Set the strategy for the organisation's data platforms and data engineering services.
Lead multidisciplinary teams that deliver data services for internal teams and health and care partners.
Advise senior leaders on data platform risks, costs, and investment.
Make sure data services meet information governance, security, and clinical safety requirements.
Build data engineering capability through recruitment, development, and career paths.
qualifications: Extensive experience of leading data engineering across multiple teams.

roles.title: Analytics engineer
roles.summary: Analytics engineers turn raw health and care data into clean, tested, and documented data models that analysts, data scientists, and reporting tools can rely on. They sit between data engineering and analysis, applying software engineering practices such as version control, testing, and code review to the transformations behind the organisation's reports and dashboards.
healthContext: Data models encode clinical and operational definitions, such as what counts as an admission, a readmission, or a breach of a waiting time standard, so definitions are agreed with clinical and operational leads.
Clinical codes from terminologies and classifications such as SNOMED CT and ICD are grouped into reference sets for analysis, which need careful version control.
Models used for performance and funding reports must be consistent and auditable, because errors can affect decisions about patient services.
Models often hold pseudonymised patient-level data, so access, documentation, and data minimisation are built in.

pcfRole.name: Analytics engineer
pcfRole.description:
An analytics engineer transforms data relevant to the organisation into structures that enable analysis and decision-making.

In this role, you will:
- work with subject matter experts to understand organisational processes and translate these into data structures optimised for analysis
- work with data users to design and build data models they can use for effective analysis and decision-making, using modelling techniques such as Kimball or Inmon
- support data quality improvement
- develop standards for data transformation
- create and maintain data documentation
- refine requirements in response to feedback from users and changes in the organisation
- provide ongoing support to users

levels.title: Trainee analytics engineer
levels.pcfLevelDescription:
A trainee analytics engineer attends training and develops skills on the job.

At this role level, you will:
- spend time shadowing other analytics engineers
- build your knowledge of the organisation
- learn skills for managing data
- learn to use different applications, tools, templates and best practices
- handle simple queries from users and document their data requirements
- contribute to data documentation and user training
responsibilities: Learn the team's data modelling tools and practices through training and pairing.
Make small, well-defined changes to data models under supervision.
Document data items and their definitions in the data catalogue.
Answer simple questions from data users and record their requirements.
Follow information governance rules when working with patient data.
qualifications: Enrolled on, or working towards, a data apprenticeship or equivalent.
levels.jobEvaluationNotes: Knowledge is scored at the level the job needs once training is complete enough to do the work.

levels.title: Analytics engineer
levels.pcfLevelDescription:
An analytics engineer develops and tests data models assigned by more senior analytics engineers to help people in a defined area access and use data.

At this role level, you will:
- draft documentation of data that meets standards
- work with other analytics engineers to resolve issues and risks
- support trainee analytics engineers
- provide training and support for users of data sets
- work with more experienced analytics engineers to develop your skills
responsibilities: Build and test data models for a service area, such as inpatient activity or community care, from agreed designs.
Write automated tests that check data models against agreed clinical and operational definitions.
Maintain reference sets of clinical codes used in analysis, with clear versions.
Document models so analysts understand their meaning, sources, and limits.
Train and support users of the team's data sets.
qualifications: A degree in a numerate or computing subject, or equivalent experience.
Experience of building data models or analytical code.

levels.title: Senior analytics engineer
levels.pcfLevelDescription:
A senior analytics engineer oversees the development and testing of data models, including directing the work of other analytics engineers.

At this role level, you will:
- oversee tasks and support less senior analytics engineers
- build relationships with stakeholders within a defined area
- coach and mentor less senior analytics engineers
- ensure documentation of data meets standards
- ensure issues and risks are resolved
- oversee training and support for users of data sets
- explore and develop new ways of working with data
responsibilities: Oversee the design and testing of data models across several service areas.
Agree definitions of key measures with clinical, operational, and finance leads, and make sure models apply them consistently.
Make sure models that feed performance and funding reports are auditable and well tested.
Resolve data issues and risks with data engineers and data owners.
Coach and direct the work of other analytics engineers.
qualifications: Substantial experience of data modelling and analytics engineering, at a level equivalent to a master's degree.

levels.title: Lead analytics engineer
levels.pcfLevelDescription:
A lead analytics engineer leads the design and deployment of data models for analysis.

At this role level, you will:
- lead and support a team of analytics engineers to design, build and maintain data models
- work with stakeholders and teams across the organisation to understand relationships between data and organisational processes, and use this to define data requirements
- promote, build awareness and support understanding of analytics engineering
- review the work of other analytics engineers
- create standards for communication, data models and documentation
- define and improve ways of working in the team
responsibilities: Lead a team that designs, builds, and maintains the organisation's analytical data models.
Set standards for data models, tests, documentation, and definitions of measures.
Work with teams across the organisation to understand how clinical and operational processes create data.
Review the work of other analytics engineers and improve the team's ways of working.
Line manage analytics engineers.
qualifications: Extensive experience of leading analytics engineering or data modelling.

levels.title: Head of analytics engineering
levels.pcfLevelDescription:
A head of analytics engineering oversees the development of a range of data models that meet analysis needs across the organisation.

At this role level, you will:
- build relationships with senior stakeholders across the organisation to determine what the organisation needs
- ensure the activities of the analytics engineering team align with strategic priorities
- ensure the team works to standards for communication, data models and documentation
- advocate for the analytics engineering role to senior leadership and other organisations
- build analytics engineering capability by providing technical leadership and career development for the community
- ensure appropriate technology is available for the community
responsibilities: Set the direction for the organisation's analytical data models, so that analysis across the organisation uses one trusted set of definitions.
Make sure analytics engineering priorities support the organisation's strategy and reporting duties.
Advise senior leaders on the trustworthiness of the data behind major reports and decisions.
Make sure the community has the tools and platforms it needs, and manage the related budget.
Build analytics engineering capability through technical leadership and career development.
qualifications: Extensive experience of leading analytics engineering across an organisation.

roles.title: Data scientist
roles.summary: Data scientists use statistics, machine learning, and other advanced methods to find patterns in health and care data and to build models that help services plan, predict, and improve care. Typical work includes forecasting demand, identifying patients who may benefit from early support, and evaluating the effect of service changes. They work closely with clinicians and analysts, and make sure models are valid, fair, and used safely.
healthContext: A model that supports decisions about patients can cause harm if it is wrong or biased, so models are validated on the population they will be used with and assessed for clinical safety.
Health data reflects unequal access to care, so models can repeat or worsen health inequalities unless bias is measured and addressed for each patient group.
Some models, such as those that inform diagnosis or treatment, may be regulated as medical devices, and AI regulation may also apply.
Data science often needs linked, detailed patient data, so work happens in secure settings, with pseudonymised data, under an agreed information governance basis.
Clinicians and patients need to understand and trust a model's outputs, so explanation and plain-language communication of uncertainty matter.

pcfRole.name: Data scientist
pcfRole.description:
Data science is a broad and fast-moving field spanning maths, statistics, software engineering and communications. Data scientists will often work as part of a multidisciplinary team, using data and analytics to inform and achieve organisational goals.

In this role, you will:
- be inquisitive
- explore and visualise data
- make recommendations to address complex problems and to inform strategic and operational decision making
- use data ethically and appropriately
- be innovative and adaptable
- explore existing and new data using a range of statistical tools and techniques, such as machine learning and predictive analytics
- find patterns in data and transform them into organisational insight

levels.title: Trainee data scientist
levels.pcfLevelDescription:
A trainee data scientist is inquisitive, curious about data and keen to learn and develop.

At this role level, you will:
- have a basic understanding of software development and analytical methods
- interpret statistical outputs effectively
- be aware of how data science techniques can be used, and have a basic knowledge of those key techniques, such as machine learning
- work as part of a multidisciplinary team to develop data science solutions and outputs
- prepare and manipulate data
- present effectively
- be aware of ethical considerations
- be aware of the technologies used
responsibilities: Learn the team's statistical and machine learning methods, tools, and secure ways of working through structured training.
Prepare and explore pseudonymised health data sets under supervision.
Run and interpret simple statistical analyses, checking results with a more experienced data scientist.
Follow information governance, disclosure control, and ethics procedures.
Work towards a data science apprenticeship or equivalent qualification.
qualifications: Enrolled on, or working towards, a data science apprenticeship or equivalent.
levels.jobEvaluationNotes: Knowledge is scored at the level the job needs once training is complete enough to do the work.

levels.title: Associate data scientist
levels.pcfLevelDescription:
An associate data scientist is inquisitive, curious about data and keen to learn and develop.

At this role level, you will:
- understand the basics of software development and analytical methods, and be able to develop basic models
- understand and be able to implement a range of data science techniques, including machine learning
- collaborate with others to develop data science solutions and outputs supporting the organisation
- prepare and manipulate data, and perform analytics
- present and communicate effectively
- be aware of project delivery methods
- be aware of ethical considerations
- have knowledge of the technologies used
responsibilities: Build and test basic statistical and machine learning models, such as demand forecasts, with guidance.
Prepare and link health data sets for modelling in secure environments.
Measure how well models perform for different patient groups and report differences.
Present results and their uncertainty to analysts and service teams.
Document data sources, methods, and assumptions so work can be reproduced.
qualifications: A degree in a numerate subject, a data science apprenticeship, or equivalent experience.

levels.title: Data scientist
levels.pcfLevelDescription:
A data scientist will work independently and have a good understanding of a range of topics, including data science techniques, delivery methods and stages (such as minimal viable products), tools and technologies.

At this role level, you will:
- develop complex solutions using a range of data science techniques, whilst understanding any ethical considerations
- understand the role and benefits of data science within the organisation
- support capability building within the organisation
- collaborate with others to develop data science solutions and outputs supporting the organisation
- prepare and manipulate data, and perform complex analytics
- present and communicate effectively
responsibilities: Develop complex models independently, such as risk stratification or length-of-stay prediction, choosing suitable methods.
Validate models with clinicians, checking that they are accurate, fair, and useful on local patient data.
Document each model's intended use, data, performance, and limits, and contribute evidence to clinical safety cases.
Evaluate the effect of service changes using suitable statistical methods.
Explain models and their uncertainty to clinical and non-technical audiences.
Support associate and trainee data scientists.
qualifications: A degree in a numerate subject, or equivalent experience.
Experience of building and validating statistical or machine learning models.

levels.title: Principal data scientist
levels.pcfLevelDescription:
A principal data scientist is a leader of data science, quite often with responsibility for managing and developing teams.

At this role level, you will:
- have a broad knowledge of data science techniques, use cases and potential impact, as well as the tools and technologies
- have extensive experience in scoping, designing and delivering data science outputs and products
- work collaboratively with a range of experts in support of organisational objectives
- communicate effectively and challenge delivery plans and priorities
- appreciate and understand data ethics, data preparation and manipulation
- appreciate and understand delivery methods, and how to deliver supported solutions at scale
responsibilities: Scope, design, and lead data science projects that support service planning and patient care.
Decide which methods, tools, and data are suitable, and challenge plans that are not feasible or safe.
Plan the validation, bias assessment, and monitoring of models with clinical safety and information governance colleagues.
Agree with product teams how models will be deployed and supported at scale.
Manage and develop a small team of data scientists.
qualifications: Substantial experience of delivering data science, at a level equivalent to a master's degree or a doctorate in a quantitative subject.

levels.title: Lead data scientist
levels.pcfLevelDescription:
A lead data scientist is a leader, coach, and champion of data science. They have responsibility for managing and developing teams, building organisational capability, and setting and communicating direction.

At this role level, you will:
- have experience in identifying opportunities to deploy extensive knowledge of data science techniques, and in challenging the status quo
- design and implement scalable data science outputs and products, driving collaboration with others in support of organisational objectives
- select the most appropriate tools and technologies
- navigate ethical and data challenges
- communicate and present effectively
- challenge delivery plans and priorities
responsibilities: Lead data science teams and set their direction, priorities, and standards.
Find opportunities where data science can improve care, and make the case for them with clinical and service leaders.
Make sure models are designed, validated, and monitored so they stay safe and fair in use.
Resolve complex ethical and data challenges, such as consent, bias, and use of sensitive data.
Build data science capability through coaching, recruitment, and training.
qualifications: Extensive experience of leading data science teams.
levels.jobEvaluationNotes: The UK GDaD PCF suggests both lead data scientist and head of data science at G7 or G6. This reference places lead at Band 8a and head at Band 8b, so the two levels sit in different bands.

levels.title: Head of data science
levels.pcfLevelDescription:
The head of data science has complete oversight of data science within their organisation.

At this role level, you will:
- set direction
- build capability
- oversee resourcing, budgeting, professionalism and outputs and products
- support and enable future IT developments
- understand and use a wide range of data science techniques, tools and technologies
- lead on ethics
- communicate and present data science and data ethics effectively to ministers and senior leaders
- champion the role of data science in supporting organisational priorities, and in collaborative working across professions
- represent the department on data science matters
responsibilities: Set the direction for data science and AI across the organisation, in line with its strategy and priorities.
Lead on the ethics, safety, and assurance of the organisation's models and AI, and advise the board on them.
Oversee resources, budget, and the quality of data science products.
Represent the organisation on data science and AI with health and care partners, researchers, and regulators.
Build data science capability and careers across professions.
qualifications: Extensive experience of leading data science across an organisation.

roles.title: Machine learning engineer
roles.summary: Machine learning engineers take models built by data scientists, or bought from suppliers, and make them work reliably in live health and care services. They build the pipelines that train, test, deploy, and monitor models, and integrate them with clinical and operational systems. They make sure models stay safe, secure, fair, and effective once real patients and staff rely on them.
healthContext: Models in live use can drift as patient populations, clinical practice, or recording habits change, so performance is monitored for each patient group and models are retrained or withdrawn when needed.
A model that informs diagnosis, triage, or treatment may be regulated as a medical device, which brings formal requirements for its software life cycle, change control, and post-market surveillance.
Clinical safety cases need evidence about how a model fails, how its outputs are shown to clinicians, and what happens when it is unavailable.
Models trained on patient data can leak information about individuals, so training data, model artefacts, and logs are protected like the data itself.
Generative AI and large language models bring further risks, such as made-up content in clinical notes, which need specific testing and human oversight.

pcfRole.name: Machine learning engineer
pcfRole.description:
A machine learning engineer develops, assures and maintains machine learning models so they can be used in products and services.

In this role, you will:
- be responsible for the software development and technical infrastructure needed to design, train, deploy and scale machine learning models
- provide and maintain effective, secure and sustainable machine learning models for use in products and services
- support all stages of the machine learning life cycle
- help product teams evaluate and choose appropriate machine learning solutions

levels.title: Senior machine learning engineer
levels.pcfLevelDescription:
A senior machine learning engineer develops machine learning models so they can be used in products and services.

At this role level, you will:
- decide what model is most suitable for use in products and services
- customise, optimise, re-train and maintain existing models
- deploy models into production, testing and assuring them to ensure they meet performance requirements
- work with others to integrate models with existing systems
- check that models used in live products and services stay safe, secure and continue to work effectively
responsibilities: Deploy models into production clinical and operational services, with automated testing, versioning, and rollback.
Build monitoring for model performance, drift, and fairness across patient groups, with alerts and clear owners.
Integrate models with clinical systems, using open standards such as HL7 FHIR where possible.
Produce the testing, change, and monitoring evidence needed for clinical safety cases and medical device technical files.
Assess and adapt supplier and open source models for local use, including generative AI models.
Coach data scientists and engineers on machine learning engineering practice.
qualifications: Substantial experience of building and running machine learning systems in production, at a level equivalent to a master's degree.

levels.title: Lead machine learning engineer
levels.pcfLevelDescription:
A lead machine learning engineer leads the technical development and deployment of machine learning models.

At this role level, you will:
- lead the most complex technical work needed to develop models for use in products and services
- co-ordinate moving a model from the research and development stage to production
- define ways of working across the machine learning life cycle
- identify training needs for machine learning engineers and related roles
- help your team work with other teams and disciplines
- assure the effectiveness of machine learning models in use across the organisation
- define and communicate software standards and guidelines related to ethics, risk and security
responsibilities: Lead the most complex work to bring models from research into safe live use across the organisation.
Define the machine learning life cycle, including the controls needed for regulated and safety-critical models.
Set standards for model testing, monitoring, security, and ethics, and assure models in live use.
Work with clinical safety officers, information governance, and regulatory specialists to agree how models are assessed and approved.
Identify training needs and develop machine learning engineers and related roles.
qualifications: Extensive experience of leading machine learning engineering for complex or regulated services.

roles.title: Data governance manager
roles.summary: Data governance managers make sure the organisation's health and care data is well managed, trustworthy, and used safely and lawfully. They set up and run the frameworks, policies, and standards for data ownership, quality, metadata, and data sharing, and work with data owners, information governance colleagues, and clinical leads so data can be used with confidence for care, planning, and research.
healthContext: Health data is highly sensitive personal data, so data governance works closely with information governance, data protection, and the duty of confidentiality.
Data is shared with many health and care partners for direct care, planning, and research, and each use needs a clear lawful basis, agreements, and controls.
Clinical data standards, such as SNOMED CT, ICD, and HL7 FHIR, and agreed data definitions are central to making data consistent across systems and organisations.
Poor data quality can lead directly to patient harm, such as missed allergies or wrong patient matching, as well as to wrong decisions about services.
Patients and the public expect openness about how their data is used, so governance includes transparency and respect for patients' choices about secondary use.

pcfRole.name: Data governance manager
pcfRole.description:
