levels.summary: A senior cyber security manager leads cyber security across several teams, manages assurance against sector standards, and runs the organisation's security improvement programme.
responsibilities: Lead cyber security teams across operations, engineering, and assurance.
Run the organisation's cyber security improvement programme and manage its budget.
Manage assurance against sector cyber security standards and ISO/IEC 27001 controls, and prepare evidence for audits.
Lead the response to major cyber incidents, and plan and test recovery with business continuity and clinical leads.
Assess the security of suppliers and shared services, and agree security requirements in contracts.
Advise programme boards on the security risks of new clinical and digital services.
qualifications: Extensive experience of leading cyber security teams in a complex organisation.
A recognised professional security certification, or equivalent experience.
levels.jobEvaluationNotes: Mental and emotional effort reflect leading the response to major cyber incidents, which can last days or weeks and threaten patient care.

levels.title: Head of cyber security
levels.summary: A head of cyber security sets the organisation's cyber security strategy and is accountable for its cyber risk management, security operations, and response to major incidents.
responsibilities: Set the cyber security strategy, in line with the organisation's digital and clinical strategies.
Advise the board and executive team on cyber risk, risk appetite, and investment.
Lead the organisation's response to major cyber incidents, including communication with regulators, partners, and the public.
Build a security culture in which all staff, including clinicians, understand threats and report them.
Represent the organisation in health care cyber security networks and with partner organisations.
Lead and develop the cyber security function, and manage its budget.
qualifications: Extensive experience of leading cyber security for a large organisation, including major incident response.

levels.title: Chief information security officer
levels.summary: A chief information security officer has corporate responsibility for cyber security across the organisation, and often across partner organisations that share its services.
responsibilities: Hold corporate responsibility for cyber security, and report on it to the board.
Set the security risk appetite with the board, and make sure it shapes decisions across the organisation.
Lead cyber security across shared services and partner organisations, where the organisation provides them.
Direct the organisation's response to the most serious cyber incidents, working with the executive team and the relevant authorities.
Shape cyber security practice across the health and care sector by working with partners and sector bodies.
Lead the security function and hold budgets across several services.
qualifications: Extensive experience of leading cyber security at board level, or for several organisations.
levels.jobEvaluationNotes: This level fits larger organisations, or those that provide shared digital services to partners. Smaller organisations usually have a head of cyber security at Band 8c as their most senior security role.

roles.title: Quality assurance test analyst
roles.summary: Quality assurance test analysts check that the organisation's digital health services do what patients, clinicians, and care staff need, safely and reliably. They analyse requirements and designs to find risks early, design and run functional and non-functional tests, and report defects clearly. In health care this includes testing clinical workflows, data accuracy, and the controls that protect patients from harm.
healthContext: Defects in clinical systems can harm patients, for example through a wrong medication dose, a missed result, or a record shown for the wrong patient, so testing is prioritised by clinical risk.
Testing provides evidence for clinical safety cases and hazard logs, so test plans trace to identified hazards and their controls.
Test data must never expose real patients, so analysts use synthetic or properly de-identified test data.
Many services exchange data with other health and care systems, so tests check messages against standards such as HL7 FHIR and the meaning of clinical codes.
Users include clinicians under time pressure, patients with a wide range of needs, and assistive technology users, so usability and accessibility testing matter.

pcfRole.name: Quality assurance test analyst
pcfRole.description:
A quality assurance test analyst interprets testing needs, creating and executing appropriate tests to ensure quality and alignment with requirements.

In this role, you will:
- plan, design and execute tests
- apply testing techniques and standards to learn about systems and mitigate risk
- analyse artefacts and prototypes
- test outcomes and record defects
- seek to improve testing practices to enhance quality and reliability
- recommend testing approaches

levels.title: Associate quality assurance test analyst
levels.pcfLevelDescription:
An associate quality assurance test analyst works with other test professionals to learn quality assurance testing and analysis techniques.

At this role level, you will:
- follow and apply test approaches, plans and strategies, under supervision
- analyse artefacts, such as user stories, prototypes, processes and designs, with support
- use basic functional and non-functional testing techniques
- increase your understanding of how to design and execute basic tests, develop reports, record outcomes and support the resolution of defects
responsibilities: Run test scripts for clinical and administrative workflows under supervision, recording results accurately.
Raise clear defect reports, including the steps, data, and screens involved.
Use synthetic test data and never use real patient data in test environments.
Learn the team's test approaches, tools, and the clinical safety process.
Take part in team ceremonies such as stand-ups, planning, and retrospectives.
qualifications: Good analytical and written skills, and some experience of testing or of working with digital systems, or equivalent.

levels.title: Quality assurance test analyst
levels.pcfLevelDescription:
A quality assurance test analyst designs and executes appropriate functional and non-functional tests. They apply multiple testing techniques to inform the approach to mitigate risk.

At this role level, you will:
- apply the most appropriate test approaches and plans based on risk
- analyse artefacts, such as user stories, prototypes, processes and designs
- determine what to test following an agreed approach
- ensure test coverage aligns with business risk
- follow appropriate standards to mitigate risk early
- execute tests, develop reports, record outcomes and support the resolution of defects
responsibilities: Analyse user stories, designs, and clinical workflows to decide what to test, based on risk to patients and services.
Design and run functional, accessibility, and usability tests, including end-to-end clinical scenarios.
Trace tests to hazards and safety controls, and provide test evidence for clinical safety cases.
Check data shown to users against source systems and agreed clinical codes.
Create and maintain realistic synthetic test data.
Track defects through to resolution and retest fixes.
qualifications: Experience of designing and running tests for digital services, or equivalent.
levels.jobEvaluationNotes: The UK GDaD PCF suggests HEO or SEO for both this level and the senior level, which maps both to Band 6. This reference places this level at Band 5 and the senior level at Band 6, so the two levels sit in different bands.

levels.title: Senior quality assurance test analyst
levels.pcfLevelDescription:
A senior quality assurance test analyst influences and guides others in test analysis, coordinating quality assurance activities in a defined area. They assess the business impact of testing outcomes and use insights to improve quality assurance processes.

At this role level, you will:
- use the most appropriate tools and techniques to analyse artefacts such as products, services, processes and change, to identify risks early
- work with others to support teams in developing approaches, plans and strategy, considering environments, data, tools and resources
- communicate chosen approaches, tools, techniques and outcomes to stakeholders
- guide others in quality assurance tools and techniques
- contribute to, and enable others to follow, quality assurance and testing standards
responsibilities: Coordinate quality assurance for a product or area, agreeing test approaches, environments, data, and tools.
Identify clinical and operational risks early by reviewing requirements, designs, and changes with clinicians and product teams.
Plan and lead user acceptance testing with clinicians and care staff.
Report test outcomes and residual risks to product owners and clinical safety officers, so they can make release decisions.
Guide other test analysts and help them follow testing and clinical safety standards.
qualifications: Substantial experience of test analysis, including in complex or regulated settings, or equivalent.

levels.title: Lead quality assurance test analyst
levels.pcfLevelDescription:
A lead quality assurance test analyst sets the strategy for test analysis and influences test analysis practices across a broad area. They develop, monitor and evaluate test analysis standards and methods, and make strategic decisions that improve test analysis in the organisation.

At this role level, you will:
- lead on setting standards and good practices across the test analysis community
- lead and guide teams across the organisation in test analysis
- define and implement test strategies
- mentor and coach other quality assurance test analysts
- negotiate and escalate major risks, issues and defects
responsibilities: Set test analysis standards and good practice across the organisation, including risk-based testing of clinical systems.
Define test strategies for major programmes, such as electronic patient record changes or new patient-facing services.
Make sure testing produces the evidence needed for clinical safety cases and, where relevant, medical device technical files.
Negotiate and escalate major risks, issues, and defects with senior product, clinical, and supplier leads.
Mentor and coach test analysts and lead the test analysis community.
qualifications: Extensive experience of leading test analysis for complex services.
levels.jobEvaluationNotes: The UK GDaD PCF suggests G7 or G6 for this level, which maps to Band 8b. This reference places it at Band 8a, level with the lead test engineer, because it leads one testing discipline rather than all testing; the head of test is at Band 8c.

roles.title: Test engineer
roles.summary: Test engineers build the automated tests, tools, and frameworks that let teams test the organisation's digital health services quickly and often. They write code to test functions, integrations, performance, security, and resilience, and build testing into delivery pipelines, so that changes to clinical and patient-facing systems can be released safely.
healthContext: Clinical systems are safety critical, so automated regression tests protect the safety controls recorded in hazard logs and are kept as evidence for safety cases.
Integrations with other health and care systems need automated tests against standards such as HL7 FHIR and HL7 version 2, often using simulated partner systems.
Clinical services run around the clock and peak at predictable times, so performance and resilience testing models real clinical demand.
Test environments must not hold real patient data, so engineers generate realistic synthetic data, including rare and edge clinical cases.
Software regulated as a medical device needs traceable, repeatable testing as part of its life cycle under standards such as IEC 62304.

pcfRole.name: Test engineer
pcfRole.description:
A test engineer designs, builds, automates and executes comprehensive, robust and maintainable test suites. They apply test engineering standards, perform exploratory testing and use diverse techniques to identify risks and improve testing efficiency and quality.

In this role you will:
- maintain automated tests in continuous integration, continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipelines
- use, develop and standardise reusable frameworks and tools following engineering practices and standards
- analyse and test artefacts such as products, services and business processes
- promote quality considerations throughout the development life cycle
- support the resolution of technical issues

levels.title: Associate test engineer
levels.pcfLevelDescription:
An associate test engineer works closely with other test professionals to learn test engineering activities and techniques.

At this role level, you will:
- contribute to and maintain technical test suites under supervision
- follow engineering practices and standards to apply test approaches, plans and strategies under supervision
- analyse artefacts such as user stories, prototypes, processes and designs with support
- support the development of reports, recording of outcomes and resolution of defects
- understand the technical tooling and engineering approach to design and execute tests
responsibilities: Write and maintain simple automated tests under supervision, following the team's engineering standards.
Run automated and manual tests and record outcomes accurately.
Help investigate and report defects, including in integrations with clinical systems.
Use synthetic test data and follow information governance rules in test environments.
Learn the team's test tools, code practices, and clinical safety process.
qualifications: Some experience of coding or testing, or enrolment on a relevant apprenticeship, or equivalent.

levels.title: Test engineer
levels.pcfLevelDescription:
A test engineer develops solutions to enable more efficient testing. They follow engineering standards to design and execute appropriate technical tests.

At this role level, you will:
- determine test scope and estimate the effort required
- select and use the most appropriate test approaches and techniques to mitigate risk
- use technical tooling and engineering approaches to design and execute tests
- develop and maintain technical test suites
- develop reports, record outcomes and support the resolution of defects
- contribute to and follow engineering practices and standards
responsibilities: Design and build automated functional, integration, and API tests for clinical and patient-facing services.
Build tests that check messages against HL7 FHIR profiles and other interoperability specifications.
Generate synthetic patient data that covers realistic and edge clinical cases.
Add tests to delivery pipelines so that safety-related checks run on every change.
Estimate test effort, report outcomes, and support the resolution of defects.
qualifications: A degree in computing or a related subject, or equivalent experience.
Experience of building automated tests.

levels.title: Senior test engineer
levels.pcfLevelDescription:
A senior test engineer is responsible for test engineering in their area. They influence, coach and guide others in test engineering, sharing best practice and standards.

At this role level, you will:
- select, use and guide others in using the most appropriate technical tooling, engineering approaches, test types and techniques to identify and address risks early
- extend, standardise and build reusable frameworks and tools that support testing
- communicate and document chosen approaches, tools, techniques and outcomes to the team and appropriate stakeholders
- contribute to and agree engineering standards
responsibilities: Lead test engineering for an area, choosing tools, frameworks, and test types that address its risks early.
Build reusable test frameworks and simulators for clinical systems and partner integrations.
Plan and run performance, load, and resilience tests based on real clinical demand.
Make sure automated tests trace to hazards and safety controls and produce evidence for safety cases.
Coach and guide other test engineers, and agree engineering standards with developers.
qualifications: Substantial experience of test engineering, at a level equivalent to a master's degree.

levels.title: Lead test engineer
levels.pcfLevelDescription:
A lead test engineer sets the strategy for test engineering and influences test engineering practices across a broad area. They develop, monitor and evaluate quality engineering standards, and make strategic improvements to quality engineering in the organisation.

At this role level, you will:
- lead a broad area in technical tooling, engineering approaches and test types and techniques to address risks early
- define engineering standards, enabling others to follow them
- lead and guide teams in quality engineering strategies and practices
- lead and guide test engineers
- escalate risks to senior stakeholders
- lead and implement continuous testing, identifying opportunities to test earlier
responsibilities: Set the test engineering strategy and standards across a broad area, including continuous testing in delivery pipelines.
Lead and guide test engineers and teams in quality engineering practice.
Make sure testing of regulated and safety-critical software meets the required standards and is traceable.
Escalate quality and safety risks to senior product, clinical, and supplier leads.
Find opportunities to test earlier and more often, and measure the effect on quality.
qualifications: Extensive experience of leading test engineering for complex services.
levels.jobEvaluationNotes: The UK GDaD PCF suggests SEO to G6 for this level, which maps to Band 7, the same band as the senior test engineer. This reference places it at Band 8a, because it sets test engineering strategy and standards across a broad area.

roles.title: Test manager
roles.summary: Test managers plan, lead, and assure testing for the organisation's digital health services and programmes. They decide how much testing is needed and of what kind, manage test teams, environments, and suppliers, and tell decision makers clearly what risks remain before a service goes live. In health care this includes making sure testing supports the clinical safety case and any regulatory requirements.
healthContext: Go-live decisions for clinical systems depend on test evidence and residual risks, which test managers report to product owners, clinical safety officers, and programme boards.
Large changes, such as electronic patient record upgrades, need testing across many departments, systems, and suppliers, and often clinical staff time for acceptance testing.
Testing must fit around clinical services, such as planning cutover tests and dress rehearsals to keep disruption to patient care low.
Regulated software and safety-critical changes need testing that meets standards such as IEC 62304 and the organisation's clinical risk management process.

pcfRole.name: Test manager
pcfRole.description:
A test manager is responsible for planning, monitoring and documenting testing. They implement a test strategy to ensure quality principles are delivered on time and within budget.

In this role, you will:
- create and implement test plans and approaches to mitigate risk
- monitor and control test activities, ensuring compliance with standards
- communicate risks and assess and report timely test status’ to stakeholders
- define metrics for monitoring and controlling test activities
- provide direction on complex testing issues, outlining and influencing delivery of projects and programmes
- identify opportunities for continuous improvement
- lead and support teams, providing coaching in good testing practices

levels.title: Test manager
levels.pcfLevelDescription:
A test manager works with a team to create appropriate test approaches and plans, considering environments, data, tools, resources, timelines, requirements and risk. They contribute to test strategies and identify opportunities for continuous improvement.

At this role level, you will:
- lead and support a team in testing activities
- determine and apply appropriate test types, techniques and standards to mitigate risk early
- manage, maintain and continuously improve test activities, ensuring compliance with regulatory and organisational standards
- identify and communicate risks
- oversee the reporting and recording of outcomes, including defects
- contribute to and agree testing standards, and enable others to follow them
responsibilities: Lead test planning for a product or programme, covering environments, data, tools, resources, timelines, and clinical risk.
Plan user acceptance testing with clinical and operational leads, and secure clinicians' time to take part.
Manage a team of test analysts and engineers, including supplier testers.
Make sure testing meets clinical safety, information governance, and regulatory requirements.
Report test progress, defects, and residual risks to product owners, clinical safety officers, and programme boards.
Improve test processes and agree testing standards with delivery teams.
qualifications: Substantial experience of test management for complex digital services, at a level equivalent to a master's degree.

levels.title: Head of test
levels.pcfLevelDescription:
A head of test sets the strategy for test quality and influences testing practices across a broad area. They develop, monitor and evaluate testing standards, practices, methods and specifications, and make strategic decisions that improve testing in an organisation.

At this role level, you will:
- lead and influence testing activities to ensure the organisation implements quality test frameworks
- select and guide the implementation of testing tools and technologies
- define good practices, standards and ways of working, continuously improving testing capability
- escalate risks to senior stakeholders
- contribute to cross-government test communities to improve test practices
- lead the organisation in adhering to test industry compliance and regulatory standards
responsibilities: Set the organisation's testing strategy, standards, and frameworks for digital health services.
Make sure the organisation's testing meets clinical safety, medical device, and other regulatory requirements.
Choose testing tools and technologies, and manage the testing budget and supplier contracts.
Advise senior leaders on quality and safety risks before major releases and go-live decisions.
Lead and develop test managers, analysts, and engineers, and build the organisation's testing capability.
qualifications: Extensive experience of leading testing across an organisation.

roles.title: Clinical informatician
roles.summary: Clinical informaticians are registered clinicians, such as doctors, nurses, pharmacists, and allied health professionals, who use their clinical knowledge to shape the organisation's digital health services. They make sure that clinical systems, data, and decision support fit the way care is delivered, are safe to use, and improve outcomes for patients and the experience of clinicians and care staff.
healthContext: The role needs current clinical knowledge, so most posts require registration with a clinical professional body and some ongoing clinical practice.
Clinical informaticians give specialised advice on how systems affect patient care, so their judgement directly affects patient safety.
They work closely with clinical safety officers, contributing clinical expertise to hazard identification and safety cases.
Good clinical data depends on consistent use of clinical terminologies such as SNOMED CT, so they help design structured records and decision support.
They act as a bridge between clinicians, care staff, and digital teams, and often lead clinical engagement for system changes.

levels.title: Clinical informatics specialist
levels.summary: Brings clinical expertise to the design, configuration, testing, and adoption of clinical systems, working within a product or programme team under the guidance of a senior clinical informatician.
responsibilities: Map clinical workflows with clinicians and care staff and turn them into clear requirements.
Design and test system content such as forms, order sets, and care plans against clinical scenarios.
Take part in hazard workshops and give clinical opinions on risks and controls.
Support clinicians and care staff to adopt new systems safely, including training and go-live support.
Check that clinical data is recorded consistently using agreed clinical terminologies.
Gather feedback and data on system use and propose improvements.
qualifications: Current registration with a clinical professional body, with experience of clinical practice.
Experience of using clinical systems in practice, or equivalent experience of digital change.
levels.jobEvaluationNotes: Patient care is scored at level 4 because the job advises on the care of patients through the design of clinical systems. Emotional effort reflects regular review of clinical records and incidents.

levels.title: Senior clinical informatician
levels.summary: Leads the clinical input to a major clinical system, product, or programme, giving specialised advice on how digital services affect patient care and safety.
responsibilities: Lead clinical design for a major clinical system or product, setting content and configuration standards.
Give specialised advice to product teams on clinical workflows, decision support, and safety.
Work with the clinical safety officer to identify hazards, agree controls, and provide clinical evidence for safety cases.
Lead clinical engagement and adoption across services, championing safe use among clinical peers.
Plan and carry out evaluations and clinical audits of system use and benefits.
Mentor clinical informatics specialists and clinicians new to digital work.
qualifications: Current registration with a clinical professional body, with substantial clinical experience.
A postgraduate qualification in clinical or health informatics, or equivalent experience.
levels.jobEvaluationNotes: Patient care is scored at level 5 for specialised advice on patient care. Research is level 3 because evaluation and clinical audit of systems are a main part of the job.

levels.title: Lead clinical informatician
levels.summary: Leads clinical informatics for a portfolio of clinical systems or a care setting, setting clinical design standards and leading a team of clinical informaticians.
responsibilities: Set clinical design standards and principles for clinical systems across a portfolio.
Lead a team of clinical informaticians, setting priorities and supporting their professional development.
Advise programme boards and senior leaders on clinical risk, benefit, and priorities for clinical systems.
Lead clinical decisions on decision support, alerts, and structured data across services.
Build networks of clinical champions and lead clinical engagement for large-scale change.
Commission and lead evaluations and use the evidence to shape the roadmap.
qualifications: Current registration with a clinical professional body, with extensive clinical experience.
A postgraduate qualification in clinical or health informatics, or equivalent experience of leading clinical informatics work.

levels.title: Head of clinical informatics
levels.summary: Leads the organisation's clinical informatics function and its clinical design authority, making sure that all clinical systems are designed, adopted, and improved with strong clinical leadership.
responsibilities: Set the clinical informatics strategy and lead the clinical design authority for the organisation.
Lead and develop the clinical informatics function, including its workforce plan and budget.
Give highly specialised advice to the executive team on the effect of digital investment on patient care.
Make sure that clinical systems meet clinical safety, terminology, and data standards.
Represent the organisation with health and care partners, professional bodies, and academic networks.
Lead research and evaluation partnerships to build the evidence for digital health.
qualifications: Current registration with a clinical professional body, with extensive clinical and leadership experience.
A master's degree in clinical or health informatics, or equivalent experience of leading clinical informatics at organisation level.
levels.jobEvaluationNotes: Patient care is scored at level 6 for highly specialised advice on patient care across the organisation's clinical systems.

roles.title: Clinical safety officer
roles.summary: Clinical safety officers are registered clinicians who make sure the health IT systems the organisation builds, buys, and deploys are safe for patients. They run the clinical risk management process, lead hazard identification, own hazard logs, and write and sign off clinical safety case reports, using clinical risk management standards such as ISO 14971 and IEC 80001-1.
healthContext: The role must be held by a registered clinician, so that safety judgements rest on current clinical knowledge and professional accountability.
Health IT can harm patients through wrong, missing, delayed, or misleading information, so the role assesses risks that are often hidden in data and workflows.
Clinical safety work runs through the whole life of a system, from design and procurement to deployment, change, and decommissioning.
Some products are also regulated as medical devices, so the role works with regulatory and quality colleagues where safety cases and device files overlap.
Safety incidents involving health IT may cause serious harm, so the role investigates incidents and makes sure lessons are learned.

levels.title: Clinical safety officer
levels.summary: Runs the clinical risk management process for a set of products or changes, leading hazard workshops, maintaining hazard logs, and writing clinical safety case reports for approval.
responsibilities: Lead hazard identification workshops with product teams, clinicians, and suppliers.
Assess clinical risks and agree controls, then check that the controls work through testing and evidence.
Write and maintain hazard logs and clinical safety case reports for products and changes.
Review supplier safety documentation for systems the organisation buys.
Investigate safety incidents involving health IT and recommend improvements.
Advise digital teams on the clinical risk management process and safety by design.
qualifications: Current registration with a clinical professional body, with substantial clinical experience.
Training in clinical risk management for health IT, or equivalent experience.
levels.jobEvaluationNotes: Patient care is scored at level 5 because the job gives specialised advice on the safety of systems used in patient care. Mental effort reflects prolonged concentration on safety documentation and evidence.

levels.title: Senior clinical safety officer
levels.summary: Leads clinical safety for a major programme or a portfolio of high-risk systems, signing off safety cases and guiding other clinical safety officers.
responsibilities: Lead clinical risk management for high-risk systems such as electronic health records, prescribing, and decision support.
Approve hazard logs and clinical safety case reports within delegated authority.
Advise programme boards on clinical risk and whether a system is safe to go live.
Lead investigations of serious safety incidents involving health IT.
Coach and quality-check the work of clinical safety officers and safety-trained clinicians.
Help improve the organisation's clinical risk management system and templates.
qualifications: Current registration with a clinical professional body, with extensive clinical experience.
Substantial experience of clinical risk management for health IT.

levels.title: Head of clinical safety
levels.summary: Owns the organisation's clinical risk management system for health IT, leads the clinical safety team, and gives the board assurance that its digital services are clinically safe.
responsibilities: Own the clinical risk management system, policy, and processes for all health IT.
Lead and develop the clinical safety team and the wider network of safety-trained clinicians.
Assure safety cases for major systems and make the final clinical safety recommendation on deployment.
Lead the response to serious safety incidents involving health IT, including with partners and suppliers.
Report clinical safety risks and assurance to the board and its committees.
Build a culture of clinical safety across digital, clinical, and supplier teams.
qualifications: Current registration with a clinical professional body, with extensive clinical and leadership experience.
Extensive experience of leading clinical risk management for health IT across an organisation.
levels.jobEvaluationNotes: Patient care is scored at level 6 because the job is accountable for the clinical safety of the organisation's health IT. Emotional effort reflects regular review of incidents involving patient harm.

roles.title: Chief clinical information officer
roles.summary: The chief clinical information officer (CCIO) is the senior clinical leader for digital. They set the clinical direction for the organisation's digital services, lead clinical informatics and clinical safety, and make sure that digital investment improves patient care, safety, and the working lives of clinicians and care staff. They are usually practising clinicians who sit on, or advise, the executive team.
healthContext: The CCIO brings clinical credibility to digital decisions, so most posts require a registered clinician who still does some clinical work.
They are the senior voice for patient safety in digital services, working with the head of clinical safety and the medical and nursing leaders.
They lead clinicians through large-scale change, such as replacing an electronic health record, where adoption and safety depend on clinical leadership.
They help balance digital ambition with the realities of clinical workload, workforce, and risk.

levels.title: Deputy chief clinical information officer
levels.summary: Leads major parts of the clinical digital agenda on behalf of the CCIO, such as a care setting, a professional group, or a large clinical system programme, and deputises for the CCIO.
responsibilities: Lead the clinical direction for a major programme, care setting, or professional group.
Lead a team of clinical informaticians and clinical leads, setting priorities and standards.
Advise programme boards and executives on the clinical risk and benefit of digital investment.
Chair clinical design and safety groups and make clinical decisions within delegated authority.
Build networks of clinical champions and lead clinical engagement for large-scale change.
Deputise for the CCIO at executive meetings and with partner organisations.
qualifications: Current registration with a clinical professional body, with extensive clinical and clinical leadership experience.
A master's degree in clinical or health informatics or leadership, or equivalent experience of leading clinical digital change.
levels.jobEvaluationNotes: Patient care is scored at level 6 for highly specialised advice on patient care across the organisation's digital services.

levels.title: Chief clinical information officer
levels.summary: The organisation's senior clinical leader for digital, accountable for the clinical direction of its digital services and for leading clinical informatics, with corporate influence over clinical safety.
responsibilities: Set the clinical digital strategy and make sure it supports the organisation's clinical and care strategy.
Advise the board and executive team on the clinical risk, benefit, and priority of digital investment.
Lead the clinical informatics function and the clinical design authority, and oversee clinical safety for health IT.
Lead clinical leaders across the organisation and its partners through large-scale digital change.
Make sure patient safety, clinical evidence, and staff experience shape every major digital decision.
Represent the organisation in professional, academic, and cross-organisation clinical digital networks.
qualifications: Current registration with a clinical professional body, with extensive clinical and senior leadership experience.
Extensive experience of leading clinical digital strategy and change at organisation level.
levels.jobEvaluationNotes: Patient care is scored at level 6 rather than 7 because the CCIO advises on, but is not usually accountable for delivering, clinical services. Financial and people responsibility are lower than other executive roles because large digital budgets and teams usually sit with the chief digital or information officer.

roles.title: Health records officer
roles.summary: Health records staff make sure that patient and corporate records are created, stored, tracked, retrieved, and disposed of correctly, whether they are on paper or in digital systems. They keep records available for care, protect them from loss and unauthorised access, and support the move from paper to digital records.
healthContext: Patient records must be available when clinicians need them, so delays or lost records can directly affect care.
Records contain highly confidential information, so staff follow strict confidentiality and access rules and may regularly read distressing content.
Most organisations hold both paper and digital records, so the role includes scanning, indexing, and managing hybrid records.
Records must be kept for set periods under retention schedules and then archived or destroyed securely, with an audit trail.
Records teams often process requests for access to health records, which have legal time limits.

levels.title: Records assistant
levels.summary: Files, retrieves, tracks, scans, and prepares records, following set procedures with supervision close by.
responsibilities: File, retrieve, and track paper records, and prepare them for clinics and requests.
Scan and index records into the electronic records system, checking quality.
Enter and update record details accurately in tracking systems.
Keep records secure and report any lost records or breaches straight away.
Move and store records safely, including boxes and trolleys of case notes.
qualifications: Good literacy, numeracy, and keyboard skills.
levels.jobEvaluationNotes: Physical skills are scored at level 3 for fast, accurate scanning and data entry. Physical effort reflects frequent moving of records.

levels.title: Records officer
levels.summary: Handles a range of records processes, some non-routine, such as tracing missing records, preparing records for access requests, and applying retention schedules.
responsibilities: Trace missing records and resolve tracking problems.
Prepare records for access requests, checking that they are complete before review.
Apply retention schedules and prepare records for archiving or secure destruction.
Check scanned records for quality and fix indexing errors.
Answer enquiries from clinicians, care staff, and patients about records.
Show new records assistants how to follow procedures.
qualifications: Experience of records or administrative work, or a level 3 qualification in business administration or equivalent experience.
levels.jobEvaluationNotes: Emotional effort reflects frequent indirect exposure to distressing content in health records.

levels.title: Senior records officer
levels.summary: Supervises a records team day to day and runs records processes such as access requests, audits, and retention reviews.
responsibilities: Supervise records staff day to day, allocating work and checking quality.
Process requests for access to health records within legal time limits, under the guidance of information governance colleagues.
Run record-keeping and tracking audits and report the results.
Keep records tracking and electronic records systems accurate and up to date.
Train staff in records procedures and confidentiality.
Investigate lost records and other incidents, and recommend improvements.
qualifications: Substantial experience of health records work, or a relevant qualification at foundation degree level or equivalent experience.

levels.title: Health records manager
levels.summary: Manages the health records service, its staff, systems, and procedures, and leads improvement, including the move from paper to digital records.
responsibilities: Manage the health records service, its staff, and its performance.
Write and maintain records procedures, in line with records management policy and standards.
Manage records tracking and electronic records systems for several services.
Lead scanning and digitisation projects and the move to digital records.
Run the retention and disposal programme and records audits.
Advise clinicians, managers, and information governance colleagues on records management.
qualifications: A degree or professional qualification in records or information management, or equivalent experience.
Experience of supervising a records team.
levels.jobEvaluationNotes: Information resources is scored at level 5 because running records systems for several services is the main duty.

roles.title: Information governance officer
roles.summary: Information governance staff help the organisation handle personal and health information lawfully, securely, and ethically. They advise teams on data protection and confidentiality, handle information rights requests, support data protection impact assessments, manage data breaches, and gather the evidence that shows the organisation meets information governance standards.
healthContext: Data protection law gives health information extra protection, so the bar for lawful use, security, and transparency is high.
Digital health services often share data across many care organisations, so information sharing agreements and data flows need careful review.
Patients and the public have legal rights to access their records and the organisation's information, with strict time limits.
Data breaches involving health information can cause real harm and distress, so incidents need fast, careful handling.
New uses of data, such as analytics, research, and AI, raise questions of consent, confidentiality, and public trust.

levels.title: Information governance officer
levels.summary: Supports the information governance team with information rights requests, incident logging, training records, and evidence gathering, following set procedures.
responsibilities: Log, acknowledge, and track information rights requests, and gather information for responses.
Log data breaches and near misses, and gather the facts for review.
Keep information governance registers up to date, such as the information asset register and data flow map.
Collect evidence for the annual information governance self-assessment.
Track staff completion of information governance training.
Answer routine information governance questions from staff.
qualifications: Experience of administrative or records work, or a foundation level qualification in data protection or equivalent experience.
levels.jobEvaluationNotes: Emotional effort reflects frequent indirect exposure to distressing content in requests, records, and breach reports.

levels.title: Senior information governance officer
levels.summary: Handles a caseload of information rights requests and incidents, and supports teams with data protection impact assessments and information sharing.
responsibilities: Handle information rights requests, including redaction and applying exemptions, within legal time limits.
Assess and investigate data breaches and near misses, and track actions to close.
Help project teams complete data protection impact assessments and describe data flows.
Draft information sharing agreements and privacy notices for review.
Deliver information governance training and briefings to staff.
Carry out access and record-keeping audits.
qualifications: A recognised qualification in data protection or information governance, or equivalent experience.

levels.title: Information governance lead
levels.summary: Gives expert information governance advice to a directorate or programme, leading data protection impact assessments and complex cases.
responsibilities: Advise product teams and services on lawful basis, consent, confidentiality, and retention.
Review data protection impact assessments for complex systems and recommend controls.
Handle complex or contentious information rights requests and internal reviews.
Investigate serious data breaches and recommend whether to notify regulators.
Review information sharing agreements with partner organisations.
Supervise and coach information governance officers.
qualifications: A recognised professional qualification in data protection or information governance, or equivalent experience.
Experience of advising on data protection in a health or care setting.

levels.title: Information governance manager
levels.summary: Manages the information governance service day to day, including its team, casework, assurance programme, and training.
responsibilities: Manage the information governance team and its casework, making sure legal time limits are met.
Plan and run the information governance assurance programme and annual self-assessment.
Write and review information governance policies and procedures.
Advise senior managers on information risks and keep the information risk register.
Lead the response to serious incidents, working with security, clinical safety, and communications colleagues.
Design and oversee information governance training for all staff.
qualifications: A recognised professional qualification in data protection or information governance, or equivalent experience.
Substantial experience of information governance in health or care.

levels.title: Head of information governance
levels.summary: Leads information governance for the organisation, setting its policy and strategy and advising senior leaders on information risk and compliance.
responsibilities: Set the information governance strategy, policies, and framework for the organisation.
Lead the information governance and records services and develop their staff.
Advise the executive lead for information risk, the board, and its committees on information risk and compliance.
Make the final decisions on complex disclosure, sharing, and breach notification questions.
Represent the organisation with regulators, auditors, and partner organisations.
Make sure new digital services, data uses, and AI are designed with privacy and transparency from the start.
qualifications: A recognised professional qualification in data protection or information governance, or equivalent experience.
Extensive experience of leading information governance in health or care.

roles.title: Data protection officer
roles.summary: The data protection officer (DPO) independently monitors the organisation's compliance with data protection law, advises on its duties, and is the contact point for the regulator and for people whose data it holds. In a digital health care organisation, the DPO gives expert advice on the lawful, fair, and transparent use of health data in products, analytics, research, and data sharing.
healthContext: Data protection law gives the DPO a protected, independent position, reporting to the highest level of management, so the role must be free from conflicts of interest.
Data protection law gives health data extra protection, and much of it is also subject to a duty of confidentiality, so the DPO advises on both.
Large-scale processing of health data, data linkage, and AI often need data protection impact assessments and, sometimes, prior consultation with the regulator.
Patients and the public expect transparency, so the DPO helps the organisation explain clearly how it uses their data.

levels.title: Deputy data protection officer
levels.summary: Supports the DPO in monitoring compliance and giving advice, leads complex casework, and deputises for the DPO.
responsibilities: Advise teams on data protection law, including lawful basis, transparency, and individual rights.
Review high-risk data protection impact assessments and draft the DPO's advice.
Monitor compliance through audits, spot checks, and reviews of records of processing.
Lead the investigation of serious data breaches and prepare notifications to the regulator.
Handle complex complaints and requests from individuals about their data.
Deputise for the DPO with senior leaders and the regulator.
qualifications: A recognised professional qualification in data protection, or equivalent experience.
Substantial experience of data protection in health or care.

levels.title: Data protection officer
levels.summary: The organisation's statutory data protection officer, independently monitoring compliance, advising senior leaders and the board, and acting as the contact point for the regulator and the public.
responsibilities: Monitor the organisation's compliance with data protection law and its own policies, independently.
Advise the board, senior leaders, and teams on their data protection duties.
Give formal advice on high-risk data protection impact assessments, and decide when to consult the regulator.
Act as the contact point for the regulator and for people whose data the organisation holds.
Oversee breach notification decisions and the organisation's response to regulator enquiries.
Report on data protection compliance and risk to the board and its committees.
qualifications: A recognised professional qualification in data protection, or equivalent experience.
Extensive experience of data protection law and practice, including in health or care.
levels.jobEvaluationNotes: Freedom to act is scored at level 6 because data protection law requires the DPO to act independently and to interpret the law and policy without instruction.

levels.title: Senior data protection officer
levels.summary: The data protection officer for a large organisation or a group of organisations that share a DPO, leading the data protection function and setting its standards.
responsibilities: Act as the statutory DPO for a large organisation or a group of care organisations.
Lead the data protection function, its staff, and its work programme.
Set the data protection framework and standards across the organisation or group.
Give the final advice on the highest-risk processing, such as large-scale data linkage and AI.
Lead engagement with the regulator, partners, and patient and public groups on data use.
Report to the board on data protection risk, compliance, and public trust.
qualifications: A recognised professional qualification in data protection, or equivalent experience.
Extensive experience as a data protection officer in a large or complex organisation.
levels.jobEvaluationNotes: Information resources is scored at level 6 because the job oversees how personal data is processed across the whole organisation or group.

roles.title: Finance officer
roles.summary: Finance officers keep the organisation's day-to-day finances accurate and under control. They process and record invoices, payments, income, and journals, reconcile ledgers and bank accounts, and help budget holders and suppliers with their queries. In a digital health care organisation much of this work involves technology suppliers, software licences, and cloud services, often paid from public funding with strict rules on how it is spent.
healthContext: The organisation spends public money, so every payment must be properly approved, recorded, and able to stand up to audit.
Many invoices are for software licences, cloud hosting, and support contracts, which need checking against contract terms, usage, and the right capital or revenue code.
Prompt and accurate payment matters, because small suppliers and care providers may depend on it.
Finance staff see personal information, such as staff expenses and payments to patients or care providers, and must handle it under information governance rules.
Fraud risks, such as false requests to change supplier bank details, target public bodies, so officers follow strict checks.

levels.title: Finance assistant
levels.summary: Finance assistants process routine financial transactions, such as supplier invoices, receipts, and expense claims, following set procedures with supervision close by.
responsibilities: Enter supplier invoices, credit notes, and receipts accurately into the finance system.
Match invoices to purchase orders and goods receipts, and chase missing approvals.
Check staff expense claims against policy and supporting receipts.
Answer routine queries from suppliers and staff by phone and email.
File and scan financial documents so they can be found for audit.
Follow financial procedures and information governance rules, and report anything unusual.
qualifications: Good numeracy and keyboard skills, gained through education or work experience.
Willingness to work towards an entry-level accounting qualification, or equivalent experience.
levels.jobEvaluationNotes: Physical skills is level 3 for the speed and accuracy of high-volume data entry. Financial resources is level 2 because the job handles payment information and checks small claims.

levels.title: Finance officer
levels.summary: Finance officers run a part of the transaction cycle, such as accounts payable, accounts receivable, or cash, resolving non-routine issues and reconciling their ledger.
responsibilities: Process a range of transactions, including payment runs, refunds, sales invoices, and journals.
Reconcile supplier statements, bank accounts, and control accounts, and clear differences.
Check that technology invoices match contract terms, such as licence numbers and billing periods.
Carry out supplier bank detail change checks and other anti-fraud controls.
Chase overdue debts and resolve disputed invoices with suppliers and budget holders.
Show new finance assistants how to do routine tasks.
qualifications: An entry-level accounting qualification, or equivalent experience of financial processing.
levels.jobEvaluationNotes: Financial resources is level 3 because the job prepares and releases payment runs and authorises payments within set limits.

levels.title: Senior finance officer
levels.summary: Senior finance officers handle the more complex financial processing and reconciliations, support month-end and year-end, and help budget holders understand their spending.
responsibilities: Prepare month-end entries, such as accruals and prepayments for annual software and support contracts.
Investigate and clear complex reconciling items and aged balances.
Prepare sales tax returns and reconciliations under supervision.
Produce standard budget reports and explain them to budget holders.
Check that spending is coded correctly between capital and revenue, and raise questions with the accountants.
Supervise and check the work of finance officers and assistants day to day.
Suggest improvements to financial procedures and system workflows.
qualifications: An intermediate accounting qualification, or equivalent experience.
Experience of financial processing and reconciliations.

levels.title: Finance team leader
levels.summary: Finance team leaders manage a transactional finance team or work as finance analysts, making sure processes are accurate, controlled, and efficient, and that reporting is ready on time.
responsibilities: Lead a transactional finance team, planning its work to meet payment, debt, and month-end deadlines.
Manage a ledger or financial process, and report its performance, such as payment times and aged debt.
Test and improve financial controls, and provide evidence to internal and external auditors.
Prepare balance sheet reconciliations and working papers for the annual accounts.
Improve processes, for example by automating invoice matching or introducing self-service for budget holders.
Train, support, and review the work of staff in the team.
qualifications: An intermediate or advanced accounting qualification, or equivalent experience.
Experience of leading or coordinating financial processes.
levels.jobEvaluationNotes: People is level 3 because the job manages a small finance team day to day. A finance analyst at this band would score people at level 2 and analytical at level 4.

roles.title: Payroll officer
roles.summary: Payroll officers make sure every member of staff is paid accurately and on time. They process starters, leavers, and changes, calculate pay and deductions, run payroll checks, and answer pay queries. In a digital health care organisation the payroll may include clinical, digital, and corporate staff on different contracts and pay rules, and it is often run on a shared or outsourced payroll system that the team must check and assure.
healthContext: Clinical staff may have complex pay, such as unsocial hours, on-call, and multiple contracts, which payroll must calculate correctly.
Pay rules and annual pay awards are often set nationally or by funders, and must be applied promptly and accurately.
Payroll is usually the organisation's largest single cost, so errors and fraud have a big effect on public money and on staff trust.
Payroll data is highly sensitive personal information, including health, family, and bank details, so information governance is central to the job.
Payroll depends on accurate data from workforce and rostering systems, so officers work closely with HR and system teams.

levels.title: Payroll officer
levels.summary: Payroll officers process pay changes and calculate pay for a group of staff, following procedures and checking their work before each payroll closes.
responsibilities: Enter starters, leavers, and contract changes into the payroll system from authorised forms.
Calculate pay, including overtime, enhancements, sickness, and family leave payments.
Apply tax, pension, and other deductions correctly.
Answer pay queries from staff and managers tactfully and confidentially.
Check payroll outputs for errors and correct them before the payroll closes.
Follow payroll controls and information governance rules.
qualifications: An entry-level payroll qualification, or equivalent experience of payroll processing.
levels.jobEvaluationNotes: Financial resources is level 3 because the job processes the pay that the organisation releases to staff. Physical skills is level 3 for fast and accurate data entry.

levels.title: Senior payroll officer
levels.summary: Senior payroll officers handle complex payroll cases, check the work of payroll officers, and help run payroll reconciliations and returns.
responsibilities: Resolve complex pay cases, such as back pay, multiple contracts, and salary sacrifice.
Recover overpayments sensitively and in line with policy.
Reconcile payroll to the ledger, and prepare tax and pension reconciliations.
Check the work of payroll officers and sign off sections of the payroll.
Test pay award and rule changes in the payroll system before they go live.
Train payroll officers and give basic pay advice to managers.
qualifications: An intermediate payroll qualification, or equivalent experience.

levels.title: Payroll team leader
levels.summary: Payroll team leaders manage the payroll team day to day, run the full payroll cycle, and make sure statutory reporting and pension returns are accurate and on time.
responsibilities: Plan and run the payroll cycle, making sure cut-offs, checks, and payment deadlines are met.
Sign off payroll checks and investigate significant variances.
Manage statutory payroll reporting and pension returns.
Manage the payroll team day to day, including workload, training, and quality checks.
Work with HR and rostering teams to improve the quality and timeliness of pay data.
Answer escalated pay queries and complaints.
qualifications: An advanced payroll qualification, or equivalent experience.
Experience of running a full payroll.

levels.title: Payroll manager
levels.summary: Payroll managers are responsible for the organisation's payroll service, whether run in house or by a provider, and assure leaders that pay is accurate, lawful, and well controlled.
responsibilities: Manage the payroll service and its team, and report on performance and accuracy.
Manage the contract and relationship with any payroll provider or shared service.
Set payroll controls, such as approval limits, exception reports, and separation of duties.
Plan for changes in pay rules, pay awards, pensions, and tax, and make sure they are applied correctly.
Lead payroll system changes and upgrades, working with system and HR teams.
Provide payroll information for budgets, forecasts, and the annual accounts.
Lead the response to payroll failures and serious errors.
qualifications: An advanced payroll qualification or a recognised accountancy qualification, or equivalent experience.
Experience of managing a payroll service.
levels.jobEvaluationNotes: Financial resources is level 4 because the job is responsible for the organisation's whole payroll, its largest cost. People is level 3 because the payroll team is small.

roles.title: Management accountant
roles.summary: Management accountants give managers the financial information and advice they need to plan, control spending, and make good decisions. They set and monitor budgets, forecast spending, cost services, and build the financial case for investment. In a digital health care organisation they work closely with digital programmes and product teams, where getting capital and revenue, whole-life costs, and value for money right is central to good decisions.
healthContext: Digital programmes are often funded from a mix of capital and revenue, ring-fenced, or time-limited funding, each with its own rules on what it can be spent on.
The move from owned systems to cloud services and subscriptions shifts costs from capital to revenue, which affects budgets, business cases, and funding bids.
Investment decisions must show value for money for public funds and benefits for patients, clinicians, and care staff, not only financial savings.
Contracts for software, hosting, and support often run for several years, so forecasts must include running costs long after go-live.
Budget holders in digital and clinical teams may not be finance specialists, so clear, practical advice is a large part of the job.

levels.title: Trainee management accountant
levels.summary: Trainee management accountants, sometimes called finance analysts, produce budget reports and analysis for a set of budget holders while working towards a recognised accountancy qualification.
responsibilities: Prepare monthly budget reports for a group of budget holders and explain the main variances.
Post month-end journals, accruals, and corrections to make sure reports are accurate.
Check that spending is coded correctly between cost centres, projects, and capital and revenue.
Collect forecast information and update forecasts with budget holders.
Build cost information for business cases under guidance.
Work towards a recognised accountancy qualification.
qualifications: A degree or intermediate accounting qualification, and working towards a recognised accountancy qualification, or equivalent experience.
levels.jobEvaluationNotes: Knowledge is scored at the level the job needs once training is far enough along to do the work. Financial resources is level 3 for monitoring delegated budgets.

levels.title: Management accountant
levels.summary: Management accountants are qualified accountants who run budget setting, monitoring, and forecasting for a directorate or group of services, and advise budget holders on their finances.
responsibilities: Lead the monthly reporting and forecasting cycle for a directorate or group of services.
Advise budget holders on spending, risks, and actions to stay within budget.
Prepare annual budgets, including staff costs, contracts, and licences.
Apply capital and revenue rules to digital spending, such as software development, licences, and hardware.
Build financial models for business cases and options appraisals.
Supervise and develop trainee accountants.
qualifications: A recognised accountancy qualification, or equivalent experience.

levels.title: Senior management accountant
levels.summary: Senior management accountants lead the financial management of a large directorate or major digital programme, including complex forecasting, costing, and business cases.
responsibilities: Lead budget setting and forecasting for a large directorate or major digital programme.
Model scenarios, such as funding changes, delivery delays, and the shift from capital to cloud subscription costs.
Lead the financial case for significant investments, including whole-life costs, benefits, and value for money.
Build service and product costing, such as the full cost of running a digital service.
Present financial performance and risks to senior managers and programme boards.
Manage a small team of accountants and trainees.
qualifications: A recognised accountancy qualification, with substantial post-qualification experience, or equivalent.
levels.jobEvaluationNotes: Financial resources is level 4 because the job sets the budget for a directorate or programme with its budget holders.

levels.title: Finance business partner
levels.summary: Finance business partners work as part of a directorate's leadership, often digital, data, and technology, turning financial information into decisions and making sure investment delivers value for money.
responsibilities: Act as the senior finance adviser to a directorate's leadership team, such as digital, data, and technology.
Lead the directorate's financial plan, linking spending to priorities, workforce, and investment.
Challenge and support leaders on value for money, including supplier spending, licence use, and cloud costs.
Lead business cases for major digital investments and represent finance at investment boards.
Make sure digital spending meets funding rules, spending controls, and capital and revenue limits.
Line manage management accountants who support the directorate.
qualifications: A recognised accountancy qualification, with extensive post-qualification experience, including business partnering.
levels.jobEvaluationNotes: Financial resources is level 5 because the job sets budgets across several services in a directorate.

levels.title: Head of management accounts
levels.summary: Heads of management accounts lead the organisation's budgeting, forecasting, and management reporting, and the team of business partners and accountants who deliver it.
responsibilities: Lead the organisation's annual budget setting and in-year forecasting.
Design management reporting, costing, and performance information for the board and executive.
Set business case and investment appraisal standards, including for digital investment.
Advise directors on financial risks, savings plans, and the choices needed to stay within funding.
Lead and develop the business partnering and management accounts teams.
Improve budgeting and reporting tools, including self-service reporting for budget holders.
qualifications: A recognised accountancy qualification, with extensive post-qualification experience, including leading a finance team.

roles.title: Financial accountant
roles.summary: Financial accountants make sure the organisation's accounts are complete, accurate, and follow accounting standards and public sector reporting rules. They manage the balance sheet, prepare the annual accounts and statutory returns, manage cash and treasury, account for assets, and work with auditors. In a digital health care organisation, much of the complexity comes from accounting for software, data assets, cloud arrangements, and multi-year technology contracts.
healthContext: Accounting for digital spending needs judgement, for example whether software development, configuration of cloud services, or licences can be treated as capital assets.
The organisation must account for public money to funders and oversight bodies, often against strict capital and cash limits.
Multi-year licence and support contracts create prepayments, commitments, and sometimes leases that must be accounted for correctly.
Intangible assets, such as software the organisation builds, need valuing, depreciating, and reviewing for impairment as products change.
External audit of public bodies is thorough and public, so evidence and working papers must be of a high standard.

levels.title: Trainee financial accountant
levels.summary: Trainee financial accountants prepare balance sheet reconciliations, journals, and working papers for the accounts while working towards a recognised accountancy qualification.
responsibilities: Prepare balance sheet reconciliations and clear reconciling items.
Post month-end and year-end journals, such as accruals, prepayments, and depreciation.
Maintain the fixed asset register, including software and hardware assets.
Prepare working papers and evidence for the annual accounts and audit.
Prepare cash flow information and bank reconciliations.
Work towards a recognised accountancy qualification.
qualifications: A degree or intermediate accounting qualification, and working towards a recognised accountancy qualification, or equivalent experience.
levels.jobEvaluationNotes: Knowledge is scored at the level the job needs once training is far enough along to do the work.

levels.title: Financial accountant
levels.summary: Financial accountants are qualified accountants who manage the balance sheet and prepare sections of the annual accounts, statutory returns, and tax returns.
responsibilities: Manage the month-end and year-end close for the balance sheet.
Prepare sections of the annual accounts and supporting notes.
Account for capital spending, including deciding which digital costs can be capitalised.
Prepare sales tax returns and advise on the tax treatment of contracts.
Answer auditors' questions and agree actions on their findings.
Supervise and develop trainee accountants.
qualifications: A recognised accountancy qualification, or equivalent experience.

levels.title: Senior financial accountant
levels.summary: Senior financial accountants lead the annual accounts process and the accounting for complex areas, such as intangible assets, leases, and cloud arrangements.
responsibilities: Plan and lead the annual accounts timetable and the external audit.
Write accounting papers on complex judgements, such as capitalising software development or cloud configuration costs.
Manage capital accounting, including asset lives, depreciation, and impairment of software assets.
Manage cash forecasting and drawdown of funding within cash limits.
Prepare statutory and funder returns, such as consolidation and capital returns.
Manage and develop a small team of financial accountants.
qualifications: A recognised accountancy qualification, with substantial post-qualification experience, or equivalent.
levels.jobEvaluationNotes: Financial resources is level 4 because the job manages the organisation's cash position and capital accounting.

levels.title: Financial accounting manager
levels.summary: Financial accounting managers run financial accounting, treasury, and tax for the organisation, and make sure controls and audit actions are in place.
responsibilities: Manage the financial accounting, treasury, and tax functions.
Own the organisation's accounting policies and their application to new types of spending, such as cloud and data services.
Manage bank accounts, banking arrangements, and the cash flow forecast.
Manage tax compliance and tax risk, including on technology contracts and shared services.
Lead the response to internal and external audit findings on financial accounting and controls.
Line manage financial accountants and treasury staff.
qualifications: A recognised accountancy qualification, with extensive post-qualification experience.
levels.jobEvaluationNotes: Financial resources is level 5 because the job manages the organisation's banking, cash, and assets across all services.

levels.title: Head of financial accounts
levels.summary: Heads of financial accounts lead the organisation's statutory reporting, financial control, treasury, and tax, and are the main contact for external auditors.
responsibilities: Lead the preparation of the annual report and accounts, and present them to the audit committee.
Advise directors and the audit committee on significant accounting judgements and new standards.
Own the financial rules, financial procedures, and scheme of delegation.
Lead the relationship with external auditors and oversight bodies on financial reporting.
Set treasury and tax policy, and manage financial risks.
Lead and develop the financial accounting, treasury, and transactional teams.
qualifications: A recognised accountancy qualification, with extensive post-qualification experience, including leading statutory reporting.

roles.title: Head of finance
roles.summary: Senior finance leaders are accountable for the organisation's financial health, financial control, and use of public money. They lead financial strategy and planning, advise the board on affordability and value for money, and lead the finance, payroll, and often procurement functions. In a digital health care organisation they shape how investment in technology and data is funded, approved, and shown to deliver benefits for patients and the health and care system.
healthContext: The organisation is funded with public money, so finance leaders are accountable to funders and oversight bodies for regularity, propriety, and value for money.
Technology investment is a large share of spending, and the balance between capital, revenue, and cloud subscription costs shapes what the organisation can afford.
Finance leaders must balance financial targets with patient safety and the quality of services that clinicians and care staff rely on.
Large technology and data contracts carry long-term commitments and supplier risks that the board must understand.
The organisation may work in partnerships across health and care, with pooled budgets, shared services, or hosted programmes.

levels.title: Financial controller
levels.summary: Financial controllers, sometimes called assistant directors of finance, lead a major part of the finance function, such as financial accounting and control or financial planning, and deputise for senior finance leaders.
responsibilities: Lead financial accounting, financial control, treasury, and transactional services, or financial planning and business partnering.
Make sure the annual accounts are delivered on time with a clean audit opinion.
Maintain an effective system of financial control, and report on it to the audit committee.
Lead the financial planning cycle and in-year financial reporting to the executive.
Advise directors on major financial decisions, including large technology contracts.
Lead and develop several finance teams.
qualifications: A recognised accountancy qualification, with extensive senior experience in public sector or complex organisations.
levels.jobEvaluationNotes: Financial resources is level 5 because the job manages budgets and financial processes across several services. Information resources is level 6 because the job owns the finance systems and data used across the organisation.

levels.title: Deputy director of finance
levels.summary: Deputy directors of finance lead the finance function day to day, deputise for the director of finance, and lead the organisation's financial strategy and medium-term financial plan.
responsibilities: Lead the medium-term financial plan and annual financial plan, linking them to strategy and workforce plans.
Lead the business case and investment approval process, including for major digital programmes.
Advise the executive and board committees on financial performance, risk, and savings plans.
Represent the organisation with funders and partners on financial matters.
Deputise for the director of finance, including at the board and audit committee.
Lead and develop the finance, payroll, and financial systems teams.
qualifications: A recognised accountancy qualification, with extensive senior experience of leading finance functions.

levels.title: Director of finance
levels.summary: Directors of finance are executive board members with corporate responsibility for the organisation's finances, financial control, and use of public money.
responsibilities: Hold corporate responsibility for the organisation's finances, financial control, and financial sustainability.
Set the financial strategy and lead the board's decisions on affordability, investment, and value for money.
Make sure the organisation spends public money lawfully, within its funding, and in line with spending controls.
Advise the board on the financial effect of strategy, including the shift to digital and cloud-based services.
Lead relationships with funders, oversight bodies, and external auditors.
Lead the finance, payroll, and procurement functions, and often other corporate services.
qualifications: A recognised accountancy qualification, with extensive experience at executive or board level.
levels.jobEvaluationNotes: Financial resources is level 6 because the job holds corporate responsibility for the organisation's finances.

roles.title: Legal assistant
roles.summary: Legal assistants and paralegals support the organisation's lawyers so that legal work is organised, accurate, and on time. They manage matters and documents, prepare contracts and bundles, research legal questions, and handle routine legal tasks. In a digital health care organisation much of the work involves technology contracts, data sharing and data processing agreements, information requests, and claims that may involve sensitive patient information.
healthContext: Legal files often contain confidential health information, such as clinical records in claims, so strict information governance applies.
Many agreements are for software, cloud services, and data sharing, so staff need to recognise the clauses that matter for patient data and service continuity.
Deadlines in claims, inquests, and procurement challenges are short and fixed, and missing them can be costly.
The organisation spends public money on external lawyers, so legal spending must be tracked and controlled.

levels.title: Legal administrator
levels.summary: Legal administrators run the legal team's administrative processes, such as matter opening, document management, registers, and invoices, following set procedures.
responsibilities: Open, update, and close matters in the matter management system.
File, format, and retrieve legal documents, keeping them secure and confidential.
Maintain contract, deed, and signing registers.
Manage diaries and key dates, and remind lawyers of deadlines.
Check and process invoices from external lawyers.
Answer routine enquiries and route requests for legal advice.
qualifications: Good administrative and keyboard skills, gained through education or work experience.
A legal administration qualification is useful but not essential.

levels.title: Legal assistant
levels.summary: Legal assistants support lawyers on a range of matters, preparing documents from templates, carrying out defined research, and managing the practical steps of contracts and cases.
responsibilities: Prepare standard agreements, such as non-disclosure and data sharing agreements, from approved templates.
